sentences.zh: 王珪王珪，字叔玠。

translations.literal: Wang Gui—Gui was his name; his courtesy name was Shu-jie.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, whose courtesy name was Shujie.

sentences.zh: 祖僧辯，梁太尉、尚書令。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Sengbian, Grand Marshal and Director of the Department of State Affairs of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengbian had served the Liang as Grand Marshal and Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 父顗，北齊樂陵郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Governor of Leling Commandery under Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been governor of Leling commandery under the Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 世居郿。

translations.literal: The family had long dwelt at Mei.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long lived at Mei.

sentences.zh: 性沉澹，志量隱正，恬於所遇，交不苟合。

translations.literal: By nature he was grave and detached; his purposes were hidden yet upright; he was content with whatever he met; and in friendship he did not join lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave and reserved by nature, with hidden but upright purposes; he was content with his lot and did not make friends lightly.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十三年，召入秘書內省，讎定群書，爲太常治禮郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui he was summoned into the Inner Secretariat to collate the classics and served as Lang of Ritual Administration in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 593, the thirteenth year of Emperor Wen's Kaihuang reign, he was summoned to the Inner Secretariat to collate the classics and appointed a ritual officer in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 季父頗，通儒有鑒裁，尤所器許。

translations.literal: His uncle Puo was a broadly learned Confucian with discernment and especially valued and approved him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Puo, a broadly learned Confucian of keen judgment, especially admired and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 頗坐漢王諒反，誅，珪亡命南山十餘年。

translations.literal: Puo was implicated in Prince of Han Liang's rebellion, was executed, and Gui fled for his life to the southern mountains for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Puo was executed for joining Prince Liang's rebellion against the Sui, Gui lived as a fugitive in the southern mountains for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，李綱薦署世子府諮議參軍事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the Pass, Li Gang recommended him and appointed him Adviser-in-Attendance of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu entered the capital region, Li Gang recommended him for appointment as adviser to the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 建成爲皇太子，授中舍人，遷中允，禮遇良厚。

translations.literal: When Jiancheng became Crown Prince, he was appointed Palace Attendant, then promoted to Junior Mentor, with excellent courtesy shown him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiancheng became crown prince, Gui was made a palace attendant and later promoted to junior mentor, receiving exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 太子與秦王有隙，帝責珪不能輔導，流巂州。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince and the Prince of Qin had a rift; the Emperor blamed Gui for failing to guide him and banished him to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince and the Prince of Qin fell out, the emperor blamed Gui for failing to guide the heir and exiled him to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 太子已誅，太宗召爲諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After the Crown Prince had been executed, Taizong summoned him and made him Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was put to death, Taizong summoned him and appointed him remonstrance grand master.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「正主御邪臣，不可以致治；

translations.literal: The Emperor once said, "A righteous ruler governing wicked ministers cannot bring order;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said, "A righteous ruler with wicked ministers cannot bring good government;

sentences.zh: 正臣事邪主，亦不可以致治。

translations.literal: righteous ministers serving a wicked ruler also cannot bring order.
translations.idiomatic: nor can righteous ministers serving a wicked ruler bring good government.

sentences.zh: 唯君臣同德，則海內安。

translations.literal: Only when ruler and ministers share the same virtue will the realm within the seas be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Only when ruler and ministers share the same purpose will the realm be at peace.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不明，幸諸公數相諫正，庶致天下於平。」

translations.literal: Though I am not enlightened, I am fortunate that you gentlemen often remonstrate and correct me, so that I may bring the realm to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not wise, I am fortunate that you gentlemen often correct me, so that I may bring peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 珪進曰：「古者，天子有爭臣七人，諫不用，則相繼以死。

translations.literal: Gui advanced and said, "In antiquity the Son of Heaven had seven remonstrating ministers; if remonstrance was not heeded, they died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Gui stepped forward and said, "In antiquity the Son of Heaven had seven remonstrating ministers; if their counsel went unheeded, they died one after another.

sentences.zh: 今陛下開聖德，收采芻言，臣願竭狂瞽，佐萬分一。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has opened your sage virtue and gathers even humble words; your servant wishes to exhaust his rash blindness and assist by one ten-thousandth.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has opened your sage virtue and gathers even humble counsel; I wish to offer whatever poor insight I have, however slight its help.

sentences.zh: 帝可，乃詔諫官隨中書、門下及三品官入閣。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved, and then decreed that remonstrance officials should enter the Privy Council together with the Central Secretariat, the Chancellery, and officials of the third rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and decreed that remonstrance officials should enter the privy council together with the Central Secretariat, the Chancellery, and officials of the third rank and above.

sentences.zh: 珪推誠納善，每存規益，帝益任之。

translations.literal: Gui was sincere in accepting what was good and always kept counsel for improvement; the Emperor trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was sincere in accepting good counsel and always offered constructive advice; the emperor relied on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 封永甯縣男、黃門侍郎，遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongning and made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate; he was then promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongning, appointed vice director of the Yellow Gate, and later promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 它日進見，有美人侍帝側，本廬江王瑗姬也。

translations.literal: Another day when he came to audience, a beautiful woman attended at the Emperor's side—she had originally been a concubine of the Prince of Lujiang, Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On another day when he came to audience, a beautiful woman stood at the emperor's side; she had originally been a concubine of Prince Yuan of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 帝指之曰：「廬江不道，賊其夫而納其室，何有不亡乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor pointed to her and said, "Lujiang was without the Way: he murdered her husband and took his household—how could he not perish?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pointed to her and said, "Lujiang was wicked: he murdered her husband and took his household into his own—how could he not be destroyed?

sentences.zh: 珪避席曰：「陛下以廬江爲是邪？

translations.literal: Gui left his mat and said, "Does Your Majesty regard Lujiang as in the right?
translations.idiomatic: Gui rose from his place and said, "Does Your Majesty regard Lujiang as in the right?

sentences.zh: 非邪？」

translations.literal: Or not?
translations.idiomatic: Or not?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「殺人而取妻，乃問朕是非，何也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "He killed a man and took his wife—yet you ask me whether it was right or wrong; what is the meaning of this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He killed a man and took his wife—yet you ask me whether that was right or wrong; what do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞齊桓公之郭，問父老曰：『郭何故亡？』

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant has heard that when Duke Huan of Qi was at Guo, he asked the elders, 'Why did Guo perish?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have heard that when Duke Huan of Qi was at Guo, he asked the elders, 'Why did Guo perish?

sentences.zh: 曰：『以其善善而惡惡也。』

translations.literal: They said, 'Because he honored the good and hated the wicked.'
translations.idiomatic: They said, 'Because he honored the good and hated the wicked.'

sentences.zh: 公曰：『若子之言，乃賢君也，何至於亡？』

translations.literal: The duke said, 'If what you say is so, he was a worthy ruler—how could he have come to ruin?'
translations.idiomatic: The duke said, 'If what you say is so, he was a worthy ruler—how could he have come to ruin?'

sentences.zh: 父老曰：『不然，郭君善善不能用，惡惡不能去，所以亡。』

translations.literal: The elders said, 'Not so. The lord of Guo honored the good but could not employ them, hated the wicked but could not remove them—that is why he perished.'
translations.idiomatic: The elders said, 'Not so. The lord of Guo honored the good but could not employ them, hated the wicked but could not remove them—that is why he perished.'

sentences.zh: 今陛下知廬江之亡，其姬尚在，竊謂陛下以爲是。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty knows why Lujiang perished, yet his concubine remains; your servant privately thinks Your Majesty regard it as right.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty knows why Lujiang perished, yet his concubine remains; I privately think Your Majesty regard it as right.

sentences.zh: 審知其非，所謂知惡而不去也。」

translations.literal: If you truly know it was wrong, this is what is called knowing evil yet not removing it.'
translations.idiomatic: If you truly know it was wrong, this is what is called knowing evil yet not removing it.'

sentences.zh: 帝嗟美其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed in admiration at his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration at his words.

sentences.zh: 帝使太常少卿祖孝孫以樂律授宮中音家，伎不進，數被讓。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Vice Minister of Rites Zu Xiaosun teach musical pitch to palace musicians; the performers made no progress and were repeatedly rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Vice Minister of Rites Zu Xiaosun teach musical pitch to palace musicians; the performers made no progress and were repeatedly rebuked.

sentences.zh: 珪與溫彥博同進曰：「孝孫，修謹士，陛下使教女樂，又責譙之，天下其以士爲輕乎！」

translations.literal: Gui and Wen Yanbo advanced together and said, "Xiaosun is a cultivated and careful gentleman. Your Majesty has him teach female musicians and then reproaches him—will not the realm come to hold scholars lightly!
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Wen Yanbo advanced together and said, "Xiaosun is a cultivated and careful gentleman. Your Majesty has him teach female musicians and then reproaches him—will not the realm come to hold scholars lightly!

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「卿皆我腹心，乃附下罔上，爲人遊説邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said angrily, "You are all my inner confidants—yet you side with inferiors to deceive your superiors and plead for others, is it not so?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily, "You are all my closest confidants—yet you side with inferiors to deceive your superiors and plead for others, is it not so?"

sentences.zh: 彥博懼，謝罪，珪不謝，曰：「臣本事前宮，罪當死，陛下矜其性命，引置樞密，責以忠效。

translations.literal: Yanbo was afraid and apologized; Gui did not apologize but said, "Your servant originally served the former palace and deserved death; Your Majesty spared his life and placed him in the inner councils, charging him with loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was afraid and apologized; Gui did not apologize but said, "I originally served the former palace and deserved death; Your Majesty spared my life and placed me in the inner councils, charging me with loyal service.

sentences.zh: 今疑臣以私，是陛下負臣，臣不負陛下。」

translations.literal: Now to suspect your servant of private motives is for Your Majesty to fail your servant; your servant has not failed Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now to suspect me of private motives is for Your Majesty to fail me; I have not failed Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 帝默然慚，遂罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent in shame and then dismissed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent in shame and then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 明日，語房玄齡曰：「昔武王不用夷、齊，宣王殺杜伯，自古帝王納諫固難矣。

translations.literal: The next day he said to Fang Xuanling, "In the past King Wu did not employ Boyi and Shuqi, and King Xuan killed Duke of Du—since antiquity it has indeed been hard for emperors and kings to accept remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he said to Fang Xuanling, "In the past King Wu did not employ Boyi and Shuqi, and King Xuan killed Duke of Du—since antiquity it has indeed been hard for rulers to accept remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 朕夙夜庶幾於前聖，昨責珪等，痛自悔，公等勿懲是不進諫也！」

translations.literal: I day and night hope to approach the former sages; yesterday I rebuked Gui and the others and deeply repented—do not let this discourage you from not remonstrating!"
translations.idiomatic: I day and night hope to approach the former sages; yesterday I rebuked Gui and the others and deeply repented—do not let this discourage you from remonstrating!"

sentences.zh: 時珪與玄齡、李靖、溫彥博、戴胄、魏征同輔政。

translations.literal: At that time Gui, together with Xuanling, Li Jing, Yanbo, Dai Zhou, and Wei Zheng, jointly assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gui, together with Xuanling, Li Jing, Yanbo, Dai Zhou, and Wei Zheng, jointly assisted in government.

sentences.zh: 帝以珪善人物，且知言，因謂曰：「卿標鑒通晤，爲朕言玄齡等材，且自謂孰與諸子賢？」

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Gui was skilled at judging men and also spoke well, therefore said to him, "You are penetrating in appraisal—tell me the talents of Xuanling and the others, and say yourself which of them you surpass in worth.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gui was skilled at judging men and spoke well, the emperor said to him, "You are penetrating in appraisal—tell me the talents of Xuanling and the others, and say yourself which of them you surpass in worth.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「孜孜奉國，知無不爲，臣不如玄齡；

translations.literal: He replied, "In diligent service to the state, knowing nothing he would not do—your servant is not the equal of Xuanling;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In diligent service to the state, knowing nothing he would not do—I am not the equal of Xuanling;

sentences.zh: 兼資文武，出將入相，臣不如靖；

translations.literal: combining civil and military ability, going out as general and entering as chancellor—your servant is not the equal of Jing;
translations.idiomatic: combining civil and military ability, going out as general and entering as chancellor—I am not the equal of Jing;

sentences.zh: 敷奏詳明，出納惟允，臣不如彥博；

translations.literal: in presenting memorials with clarity and detail, in intake and output with sole fairness—your servant is not the equal of Yanbo;
translations.idiomatic: in presenting memorials with clarity and detail, in intake and output with sole fairness—I am not the equal of Yanbo;

sentences.zh: 濟繁治劇，眾務必舉，臣不如胄；

translations.literal: in managing the complex and governing the urgent, in all affairs surely accomplishing—your servant is not the equal of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: in managing the complex and governing the urgent, in all affairs surely accomplishing—I am not the equal of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 以諫諍爲心，恥君不及堯、舜，臣不如征。

translations.literal: with remonstrance as his heart, ashamed if his lord did not reach Yao and Shun—your servant is not the equal of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: with remonstrance as his heart, ashamed if his lord did not reach Yao and Shun—I am not the equal of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 至激濁揚清，疾惡好善，臣於數子有一日之長。」

translations.literal: But in stirring the muddy and raising the clear, in hating evil and loving good—your servant has one day's advantage over these several men.
translations.idiomatic: But in stirring the muddy and raising the clear, in hating evil and loving good—I have a slight edge over these several men.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his answer.

sentences.zh: 而玄齡等亦以爲盡己所長，謂之確論。

translations.literal: And Xuanling and the others also thought he had exhausted their strengths and called it a sound judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling and the others also thought he had fairly stated their strengths and called it a sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 進封郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in rank to duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 坐漏禁近語，左除同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was punished for leaking words from within the forbidden precincts and demoted to the left as Governor of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for leaking words from within the forbidden precincts and demoted to governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝念名臣，俄召拜禮部尚書兼魏王泰師。

translations.literal: The Emperor, remembering a renowned minister, soon summoned him and appointed him Minister of Rites and concurrently Tutor to Prince Wei Tai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering a renowned minister, soon summoned him and appointed him minister of rites and concurrently tutor to Prince Wei Tai.

sentences.zh: 王見之，爲先拜，珪亦以師自居。

translations.literal: When the prince saw him, he bowed first; Gui also took the position of teacher upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince saw him, he bowed first; Gui also took the position of teacher upon himself.

sentences.zh: 王問珪何以爲忠孝，珪曰：「陛下，王之君，事思盡忠；

translations.literal: The prince asked Gui what constituted loyalty and filial piety; Gui said, "Your Majesty is the prince's lord—in affairs think to exhaust loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked Gui what constituted loyalty and filial piety; Gui said, "Your Majesty is the prince's lord—in affairs think to exhaust loyalty;

sentences.zh: 陛下，王之父，事思盡孝。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is the prince's father—in affairs think to exhaust filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is the prince's father—in affairs think to exhaust filial piety.

sentences.zh: 忠孝可以立身，可以成名。」

translations.literal: Loyalty and filial piety can establish the person and can establish a name.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and filial piety can establish the person and can establish a name.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「忠孝既聞命矣，願聞所習。」

translations.literal: The prince said, "I have received instruction on loyalty and filial piety; I wish to hear what I should practice."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "I have received instruction on loyalty and filial piety; I wish to hear what I should practice."

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「漢東平王蒼稱『爲善最樂』，願王志之。」

translations.literal: Gui said, "Prince Cang of Dongping in Han said, 'Doing good is the greatest joy'—may the prince keep this in mind."
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "Prince Cang of Dongping in Han said, 'Doing good is the greatest joy'—may the prince keep this in mind."

sentences.zh: 帝聞，喜曰：「兒可以無過矣！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he said with joy, "The boy may be without fault!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he said with joy, "The boy may be without fault!"

sentences.zh: 子敬直，尚南平公主。

translations.literal: His son Jingzhi married Princess Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingzhi married Princess Nanping.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸主下嫁，以帝女貴，未嘗行見舅姑禮。

translations.literal: At that time when princesses married down, because the emperor's daughter was esteemed, they had never performed the rite of seeing father-in-law and mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At that time when princesses married down, because an emperor's daughter was deemed too exalted, they had never performed the rite of seeing their parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「主上循法度，吾當受公主謁見。

translations.literal: Gui said, "The sovereign follows law and regulation; I ought to receive the princess's visit of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "The sovereign follows law and regulation; I ought to receive the princess's visit of respect.

sentences.zh: 豈爲身榮，將以成國家之美。」

translations.literal: It is not for personal glory but to complete the state's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: It is not for personal glory but to complete the state's beauty.

sentences.zh: 於是，與夫人坐堂上，主執笄盥饋乃退。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and his wife sat in the hall; the princess took the hairpin, performed the washing, and presented food before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he and his wife sat in the hall; the princess took the hairpin, performed the washing, and presented food before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 其後公主降，有舅姑者，備婦禮，本於珪。

translations.literal: Afterward when princesses married down, if there were parents-in-law, they prepared the wife's rites—this originated with Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward when princesses married down, if there were parents-in-law, they prepared the wife's rites—this originated with Gui.

sentences.zh: 十三年，病。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 帝遣公主就第省視，復遣民部尚書唐儉增損藥膳。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the princess to his residence to visit him and also sent Minister of Revenue Tang Jian to adjust his medicines and food.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the princess to his residence to visit him and also sent Minister of Revenue Tang Jian to adjust his medicines and food.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝素服哭別次，詔魏王率百官臨哭。

translations.literal: The Emperor in plain dress wept at a separate lodge and decreed that the Prince of Wei should lead the hundred officials to attend the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in plain dress wept at a separate lodge and decreed that the Prince of Wei should lead the hundred officials to attend the mourning.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Personnel; his posthumous title was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of personnel; his posthumous title was Yi.

sentences.zh: 珪少孤且貧，人或饋遺，初無讓。

translations.literal: Gui was orphaned young and poor; when people gave him gifts, at first he did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was orphaned young and poor; when people gave him gifts, at first he did not decline.

sentences.zh: 及貴，厚報之，雖已亡，必酬贍其家。

translations.literal: When he became eminent he repaid them generously; even if they had died, he surely compensated and supported their families.
translations.idiomatic: When he became eminent he repaid them generously; even if they had died, he surely compensated and supported their families.

sentences.zh: 性不苛察，臨官務舉綱維，去甚不可者，至僕妾亦不見喜慍。

translations.literal: By nature he was not harsh in scrutiny; in office he strove to raise the main cords, removing only what could not be tolerated—even toward servants and concubines he showed no joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was not harsh in scrutiny; in office he strove to uphold essentials, removing only what could not be tolerated—even toward servants and concubines he showed no joy or anger.

sentences.zh: 奉寡嫂，家事咨而後行。

translations.literal: He served his widowed sister-in-law; on household affairs he consulted her before acting.
translations.idiomatic: He served his widowed sister-in-law; on household affairs he consulted her before acting.

sentences.zh: 教撫孤侄，雖其子不過也。

translations.literal: He taught and nurtured his orphaned nephews, not treating them less than his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: He taught and nurtured his orphaned nephews, not treating them less than his own sons.

sentences.zh: 宗族匱乏，周恤之，薄於自奉。

translations.literal: When clansmen were in want, he relieved them roundly and was sparing in his own maintenance.
translations.idiomatic: When clansmen were in want, he relieved them generously and was sparing in his own maintenance.

sentences.zh: 獨不作家廟，四時祭於寢，爲有司所劾，帝爲立廟愧之，不罪也。

translations.literal: He alone did not build a family temple but sacrificed at the four seasons in his bedchamber; the authorities impeached him, and the Emperor built a temple for him out of shame on his behalf and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: He alone did not build a family temple but sacrificed at the four seasons in his bedchamber; the authorities impeached him, and the emperor built a temple for him out of shame on his behalf and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 世以珪儉不中禮，少之。

translations.literal: The age thought Gui's frugality did not accord with ritual and slighted him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The age thought Gui's frugality did not accord with ritual and slighted him for it.

sentences.zh: 始，隱居時，與房玄齡、杜如晦善，母李嘗曰：「而必貴，然未知所與遊者何如人，而試與偕來。」

translations.literal: At the beginning, while in seclusion, he was on good terms with Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui; his mother Lady Li once said, "You will surely become eminent, yet I do not know what sort of men those you associate with are—bring them to try them with me.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, while in seclusion, he was on good terms with Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui; his mother Lady Li once said, "You will surely become eminent, yet I do not know what sort of men those you associate with are—bring them to try them with me.

sentences.zh: 會玄齡等過其家，李窺大驚，敕具酒食，歡盡日，喜曰：「二客公輔才，汝貴不疑。」

translations.literal: When Xuanling and the others happened to pass his home, Lady Li peered out and was greatly startled; she ordered wine and food prepared, and they rejoiced the whole day; she said with joy, "These two guests have the talent of chief ministers—your eminence is beyond doubt."
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanling and the others happened to pass his home, Lady Li peered out and was greatly startled; she ordered wine and food prepared, and they rejoiced the whole day; she said with joy, "These two guests have the talent of chief ministers—your eminence is beyond doubt."

sentences.zh: 敬直封南城縣男，後坐交皇太子承乾，徙嶺外。

translations.literal: Jingzhi was enfeoffed as Baron of Nancheng; later he was punished for associating with Crown Prince Chengan and was banished beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi was enfeoffed as Baron of Nancheng; later he was punished for associating with Crown Prince Chengan and was banished beyond the ranges.

sentences.zh: 珪孫燾、旭。

translations.literal: Gui's grandsons were Tao and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's grandsons were Tao and Xu.

sentences.zh: 珪孫 燾燾，性至孝，爲徐州司馬。

translations.literal: Gui's grandson Tao—Tao was by nature supremely filial and served as Vice Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's grandson Tao was supremely filial by nature and served as vice governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 母有疾，彌年不廢帶，視絮湯劑。

translations.literal: When his mother was ill, for a full year he did not remove his belt and personally attended to her bedding and medicines.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was ill, for a full year he did not remove his belt and personally attended to her bedding and medicines.

sentences.zh: 數從高醫遊，遂窮其術，因以所學作書，號《外臺秘要》，討繹精明，世寶焉。

translations.literal: He often associated with eminent physicians and thoroughly mastered their arts; accordingly he wrote a book from what he had learned, titled Essentials from the Outer Terrace, with exposition refined and penetrating—the age treasures it.
translations.idiomatic: He often associated with eminent physicians and thoroughly mastered their arts; accordingly he wrote a book from what he had learned, titled Essentials from the Outer Terrace, with exposition refined and penetrating—the age treasures it.

sentences.zh: 歴給事中、鄴郡太守，治聞於時。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Within the Yellow Gate and Governor of Ye Commandery; his governance was renowned in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant within the Yellow Gate and governor of Ye commandery; his governance was renowned in his time.

sentences.zh: 旭，見《酷吏傳》。

translations.literal: Xu is treated in the Biography of Harsh Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Xu is treated in the Biography of Harsh Officials.

sentences.zh: 薛收薛收，字伯褒。

translations.literal: Xue Shou—Shou was his name; his courtesy name was Bo-bao.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shou, whose courtesy name was Bobao.

sentences.zh: 蒲州汾陰人。

translations.literal: He was a man of Fenyin in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was a native of Fenyin in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋內史侍郎道衡子也，出繼從父孺。

translations.literal: He was the son of Daoheng, Vice Director of the Inner Secretariat of Sui, and was given in adoption to his father's younger cousin Ru.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Daoheng, vice director of the inner secretariat of Sui, and was given in adoption to his father's younger cousin Ru.

sentences.zh: 年十二，能屬文。

translations.literal: At twelve he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could compose literary pieces.

sentences.zh: 以父不得死於隋，不肯仕。

translations.literal: Because his father had not been permitted to die for Sui, he refused to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had not been permitted to die for Sui, he refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 郡舉秀才，不應。

translations.literal: The commandery recommended him as Presented Scholar; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery recommended him as presented scholar; he did not respond.

sentences.zh: 聞高祖興，遁入首陽山，將應義舉。

translations.literal: When he heard that Gaozu had risen, he fled into Mount Shouyang, intending to respond to the righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Gaozu had risen, he fled into Mount Shouyang, intending to join the righteous rising.

sentences.zh: 通守堯君素覺之，迎置其母城中，收不得去。

translations.literal: Circuit Administrator Yao Junsu detected him, welcomed his mother into the city, and Shou could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit administrator Yao Junsu detected him, welcomed his mother into the city, and Shou could not leave.

sentences.zh: 及君素東連王世充，遂挺身歸國。

translations.literal: When Junsu linked eastward with Wang Shichong, he then threw himself forward and returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Junsu linked eastward with Wang Shichong, he then threw himself forward and returned to the Tang cause.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡亟言之秦王，王召見，問方略。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling repeatedly spoke of him to the Prince of Qin; the Prince summoned him for an audience and asked about strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling urged the Prince of Qin again and again to see him. The Prince called him in and questioned him on plans of war.

sentences.zh: 所對合旨，授府主簿，判陝東大行臺金部郎中。

translations.literal: What he answered accorded with the Prince's intent; he was appointed Master of Records of the princely household and concurrently served as Lang of the Gold Department of the Eastern Shaanxi Grand Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His answers hit the mark. The Prince made him Master of Records in his household and put him in charge of the Gold Department under the Eastern Shaanxi Grand Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是時方討世充，軍事繁綜，收爲書檄露布，或馬上占辭，該敏如素構，初不竄定。

translations.literal: At that time they were just campaigning against Shichong; military affairs were complex and manifold. Shou drafted letters, proclamations, and battle reports, sometimes composing on horseback; his work was comprehensive and quick, as if long prepared, and at first never needed revision.
translations.idiomatic: They were then pressing the campaign against Wang Shichong, and the military burden was heavy. Shou wrote dispatches and field bulletins, sometimes drafting on horseback—apt and swift, as though the words had always been there, never needing a second pass.

sentences.zh: 竇建德來援，諸將爭言斂軍以觀賊形勢，收獨曰：「不然。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande came to reinforce, the generals all argued that the army should be drawn in to observe the enemy's situation; Shou alone said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande marched to the rescue, the generals all urged pulling back to watch how the enemy shaped up. Shou alone said, "No.

sentences.zh: 世充據東都，府庫盈衍，其兵皆江淮選卒，正苦乏食爾，是以求戰不得，爲我所持。

translations.literal: Shichong holds the Eastern Capital; his storehouses overflow. His troops are picked soldiers from the Jiang-Huai region, and they suffer precisely from lack of food. That is why they cannot obtain the battle they seek and are held fast by us.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong holds Luoyang, his granaries are full, and his men are elite troops from the Jiang-Huai—but they are starving. That is why they cannot force a fight and remain pinned by us.

sentences.zh: 今建德身總眾以來，必飛轂轉糧，更相資哺。

translations.literal: Now Jiande has come in person leading his host; he must rush wagons to transport grain, each side feeding the other.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jiande has come at the head of his army himself. He will have to fly grain wagons back and forth, and the two armies will sustain each other.

sentences.zh: 兩賊連固，則伊、洛間勝負未可歲月定也。

translations.literal: If the two rebels link up and hold firm, then between the Yi and Luo rivers victory and defeat cannot be settled within months.
translations.idiomatic: If the two rebel forces join and dig in, the outcome between the Yi and Luo may not be decided for months.

sentences.zh: 不若勒諸將嚴兵締壘，浚其溝防，戒毋出兵。

translations.literal: Better to order the generals to tighten their troops and fortify their camps, deepen the ditches and defenses, and forbid any sortie.
translations.idiomatic: Better to have the generals drill their men, seal the camps, deepen the moats and ramparts, and forbid anyone to sally out.

sentences.zh: 大王親督精銳據成皋，厲兵按甲，邀建德路。

translations.literal: Your Highness should personally lead crack troops to hold Chenggao, sharpen weapons and hold ranks in readiness, and intercept Jiande on his route.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should take the picked troops in hand, seize Chenggao, keep the army ready under arms, and cut off Jiande on the road.

sentences.zh: 彼以疲老，當吾堂堂之鋒，一戰必舉。

translations.literal: They will come weary and worn against our bold, ordered edge; one battle will surely carry the day.
translations.idiomatic: They will meet our fresh, disciplined line with tired, aging men—one stroke and they will fall.

sentences.zh: 不旬日，二賊可縛致麾下矣。」

translations.literal: Within ten days, both rebels can be bound and brought beneath your banners."
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days both enemies can be bound and delivered into your hands."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Prince said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 遂禽建德，降世充。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiande was captured and Shichong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was taken, and Shichong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 王入觀隋宮室，且歎煬帝無道，殫人力以事誇侈。

translations.literal: The Prince entered to view the Sui palace halls and sighed that Emperor Yang was devoid of the Way, exhausting human labor in the service of boastful extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince toured the Sui palaces and lamented that Emperor Yang had abandoned the Way, wasting the people's strength on empty display.

sentences.zh: 收進曰：「峻宇雕牆，殷辛以亡；

translations.literal: Shou stepped forward and said, "Lofty halls and carved walls brought King Xin of Shang to ruin;
translations.idiomatic: Shou advanced and said, "Towering halls and painted walls ruined King Xin of Shang;

sentences.zh: 土階茅茨，唐堯以昌。

translations.literal: earthen steps and thatched roofs brought Tang Yao to flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: earthen steps and a thatched roof made Tang Yao prosper.

sentences.zh: 始皇興阿房而秦禍速，文帝罷露臺而漢祚永。

translations.literal: The First Emperor raised Epang and Qin's disaster came swiftly; Emperor Wen abandoned the Terrace of Dew and Han's mandate endured long.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor built Epang and Qin perished in haste; Emperor Wen stopped work on the Terrace of Dew and Han endured.

sentences.zh: 後主曾不是察，奢虐是矜，死一夫之手，爲後世笑，何此之能保哉？」

translations.literal: The Last Ruler never reflected on this but took pride in luxury and cruelty; he died at the hands of a single man and became the laughter of later ages—how could such things be preserved?"
translations.idiomatic: The Last Ruler of Chen never took this to heart, but gloried in cruelty and excess. He died by one man's hand and became a laughingstock for ages to come—how could such a house endure?"

sentences.zh: 王重其言。

translations.literal: The Prince regarded his words highly.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince weighed his words heavily.

sentences.zh: 俄授天策府記室參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Secretary in the Heavenly Stratagem Office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Secretary in the Heavenly Stratagem Office.

sentences.zh: 從平劉黑闥，封汾陰縣男。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Liu Heitu and was ennobled as Baron of Fenyin County.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in crushing Liu Heitu and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fenyin County.

sentences.zh: 嘗上書諫王止畋獵，王答曰：「覽所陳，知成我者，卿也。

translations.literal: Once he submitted a memorial advising the Prince to cease hunting; the Prince replied, "Having read what you set forth, I know that the one who completes me is you.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized the Prince to stop hunting. The Prince answered, "Reading what you wrote, I see that you are the one who makes me whole.

sentences.zh: 明珠兼乘，未若一言，今賜黃金四十鋌。」

translations.literal: Clear pearls and paired steeds are not the equal of a single word—now I bestow upon you forty ingots of gold."
translations.idiomatic: Bright pearls and matched horses are worth less than one true word. I now give you forty ingots of gold."

sentences.zh: 武德七年，寢疾。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wude, he took to bed with illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wude he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 王遣使臨問，相望於道。

translations.literal: The Prince sent envoys to visit him in his illness; they met one another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince sent messengers to inquire after him, and they passed one another on the road.

sentences.zh: 命輿疾至府，親舉袂撫之，論敘生平，感激涕泗。

translations.literal: He ordered Shou brought by litter though ill to the princely residence, personally raised his sleeve to touch him, spoke of their shared lives, and wept with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: He had Shou carried by litter to the palace though he was sick, lifted his own sleeve to touch him, talked over their lives together, and wept until the tears ran.

sentences.zh: 卒，年三十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 王哭之慟，與其從兄子元敬書曰：「吾與伯褒共軍旅間，何嘗不驅馳經略，款曲襟抱，豈期一朝成千古也。

translations.literal: The Prince wept for him in deep grief and wrote to his cousin's son Yuanjing: "I and Bobao shared the camp together—when did we not ride forth in planning and open our hearts in trust? Who expected that in a single morning it would become an eternal parting?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince mourned him bitterly and wrote to his clansman's son Yuanjing: "Bobao and I shared the hardships of camp life. When did we not ride out together to plan campaigns and speak freely from the heart? Who thought one morning would part us forever?

sentences.zh: 且家素貧而子幼，善撫安之，以慰吾懷。」

translations.literal: Moreover, his family has long been poor and his son is young—treat them well and comfort them, to ease my heart."
translations.idiomatic: His house has always been poor and his son is still young. Be kind to them and keep them safe, to comfort me."

sentences.zh: 因遣使弔祭，贈帛三百段。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice, and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to mourn and offer sacrifice, and gave three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其後圖學士像，歎其早死不得與。

translations.literal: Later, when painting the portraits of the Literary Scholars, he sighed that Shou's early death kept him from being included.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the portraits of the Literary Scholars were painted, he sighed that Shou's early death had kept him from joining them.

sentences.zh: 既即位，語房玄齡曰：「收若在，朕當以中書令處之。」

translations.literal: After ascending the throne, he said to Fang Xuanling: "If Shou were still alive, I would place him as Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Once he had taken the throne, he told Fang Xuanling, "If Shou were alive, I would have made him Grand Councilor."

sentences.zh: 又嘗夢收如平生，賜其家粟、帛。

translations.literal: He also once dreamed of Shou as in life and bestowed grain and silk upon his family.
translations.idiomatic: He also dreamed of Shou as in life and gave his family grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，贈定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, Shou was posthumously appointed Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he was posthumously made Governor of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，又贈太常卿，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: During the Yonghui era, he was further posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies and granted burial near Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonghui period he was again honored as Minister of Ceremonies and buried beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 收子 元超子元超，九歲襲爵。

translations.literal: Shou's son Yuanchao: Yuanchao, at nine years of age inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's son Yuanchao inherited the title at nine.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown, he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he loved study and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 尚巢王女和靜縣主，累授太子舍人。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Hejing, daughter of Prince Chao, and was repeatedly appointed Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Hejing, daughter of Prince Chao, and rose through several posts as Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，遷給事中，數上書陳當世得失，帝嘉納。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended, he was transferred to Drafting Censor and repeatedly submitted memorials on the gains and failings of the age; the Emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, he was moved to Drafting Censor and often wrote in on the rights and wrongs of the day. The emperor praised and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 轉中書舍人、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Secretary of the Central Secretariat and Scholar of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Drafting Secretary of the Central Secretariat and a Scholar of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 省中有磐石，道衡爲侍郎時，常據以草制，元超每見，輒泫然流涕。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat there was a boulder on which Daoheng, when Vice Minister, had often sat to draft edicts; whenever Yuanchao saw it, he would weep profusely.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat stood a great stone on which Daoheng, when he was Vice Minister, had often sat to draft edicts. Each time Yuanchao saw it, he wept.

sentences.zh: 以母喪解，奪服授黃門侍郎、檢校太子左庶子。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of his mother's mourning, but before the mourning period ended was appointed Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate and Acting Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother, but before the mourning was finished was recalled as Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate and Acting Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 所薦豪俊士，若任希古、高智周、郭正一、王義方、孟利貞、鄭祖玄、鄧玄挺、崔融等，皆以才自名於時。

translations.literal: The outstanding men he recommended—Ren Xigu, Gao Zhizhou, Guo Zhengyi, Wang Yifang, Meng Lizhen, Zheng Zuxuan, Deng Xunting, Cui Rong, and others—all made names for themselves by their talent in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Among the able men he recommended—Ren Xigu, Gao Zhizhou, Guo Zhengyi, Wang Yifang, Meng Lizhen, Zheng Zuxuan, Deng Xunting, Cui Rong, and others—each won fame in his day for talent.

sentences.zh: 累拜東臺侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Eastern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to Vice Minister of the Eastern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 李義府流巂州，舊制，流人不得乘馬，元超爲請，坐貶簡州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Yifu was exiled to Xizhou; by old regulation exiles might not ride horses; Yuanchao pleaded on his behalf and was punished by demotion to Prefect of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yifu was banished to Xizhou, old rules forbade exiles to ride horses. Yuanchao pleaded for him and was demoted to prefect of Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，又坐與上官儀文章款密，流巂州。

translations.literal: After a year and more, he was again punished for being on intimate literary terms with Shangguan Yi and was exiled to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was punished again for close literary ties with Shangguan Yi and sent into exile at Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 上元初，赦還，拜正諫大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era, he was pardoned and returned, and appointed Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shangyuan reign he was pardoned and recalled, and made remonstrance grand master.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷中書侍郎、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat and made Third Rank at the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became vice minister of the Central Secretariat and a third-rank participant in the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 帝校獵溫泉，諸蕃酋長得持弓矢從。

translations.literal: The Emperor hunted at the Hot Springs; chieftains of various foreign peoples were allowed to carry bows and arrows in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor hunted at the Hot Springs, chieftains of the frontier peoples were permitted to carry bows and arrows in the chase.

sentences.zh: 元超奏：「夷狄野心，而使挾兵在圍中，非所宜。」

translations.literal: Yuanchao memorialized: "Barbarians harbor wild hearts; to let them bear arms within the hunting enclosure is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao submitted: "The hearts of the barbarians are untamed. To let them carry weapons inside the hunting grounds is unwise."

sentences.zh: 帝納可。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘗宴諸王，召元超與，從容謂曰：「任卿中書，寧藉多人哉！」

translations.literal: Once, feasting the princes, he summoned Yuanchao and said at ease: "In placing you in charge of the Central Secretariat, do I need many others?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, while feasting the princes, he called Yuanchao to him and said lightly, "With you at the Central Secretariat, do I need a crowd?"

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書令兼左庶子。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat and concurrently Left Subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuanchao was made grand councilor of the Central Secretariat and left subordinate as well.

sentences.zh: 帝幸東都，留輔太子監國，手敕曰：「朕留卿，若失一臂。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited the Eastern Capital and left Yuanchao to assist the Heir Apparent in governing the realm; in a handwritten edict he said: "In leaving you behind, it is as if I have lost an arm.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to the Eastern Capital, he left Yuanchao to assist the heir apparent in governing the realm. In his own hand he wrote, "Leaving you behind is like losing an arm.

sentences.zh: 顧太子未習庶務，關中事，卿悉專之。」

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent is not yet practiced in common affairs—for matters in Guanzhong, you shall have full charge."
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent is still unused to the business of state. For all affairs in Guanzhong, you alone shall decide."

sentences.zh: 時太子射獵，詔得入禁御，故太子稍怠政事。

translations.literal: At that time the Heir Apparent went hunting with bow; an edict permitted entry into the forbidden precincts, so the Heir Apparent gradually slackened in affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the heir apparent was out hunting. An edict allowed him into the forbidden park, and he slowly let state affairs slide.

sentences.zh: 元超諫曰：「內苑之地，繚叢薄，冒翳薈，絶磴險途。

translations.literal: Yuanchao remonstrated: "The inner parklands are tangled with thickets, overgrown and shadowed, with steep tracks and perilous paths.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao remonstrated: "The inner park is dense with brush and shadow, its paths steep and dangerous.

sentences.zh: 殿下截輕禽，逐狡兔，銜橛之變，詎無可虞？

translations.literal: Your Highness shoots at light birds and chases cunning hares—in such a moment when the bit meets the cheekpiece, is there nothing to fear?
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness brings down small birds and runs down clever hares—if the bridle should jerk or the horse bolt, what then?

sentences.zh: 又戸奴多反逆餘族，或夷狄遺醜，使凶謀竊發，將何以禦哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, many household slaves are remnants of rebel clans, or leftover villains among foreigners—if wicked plots should break out secretly, with what will you defend yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, many of the household slaves are kin of rebels, or the dregs of foreign tribes. If treachery should break out in secret, how would you defend yourself?

sentences.zh: 夫爲人子者，不登高，不臨深，謂其近危辱也。

translations.literal: For one who is a son, not to climb high and not to stand at the brink means to keep clear of peril and disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: A dutiful son does not climb high or stand at the edge—that is, he keeps away from danger and shame.

sentences.zh: 天皇所賜書戒丁甯，惟殿下罷馳射之勞，留情墳典，豈不美歟！」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's gift of written admonitions was earnest in the extreme—if Your Highness would only leave off the labor of galloping and shooting and fix your mind upon the classics, would that not be splendid!"
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's letter of warning was full and earnest. If Your Highness would leave off riding and shooting and turn your heart to the classics, would that not be fine?"

sentences.zh: 帝知之，遣使厚賜慰其意，召太子還東都。

translations.literal: The Emperor learned of this, sent envoys with rich gifts to comfort him in his intent, and summoned the Heir Apparent back to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he sent rich gifts to comfort Yuanchao and recalled the heir apparent to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 帝疾劇，政出武后。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's illness grew severe, government issued from Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness turned grave, power passed to Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 因陽喑，乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He therefore feigned muteness and begged to retire his bones.
translations.idiomatic: He then pretended to be mute and asked to resign on grounds of age and infirmity.

sentences.zh: 加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was made Honorary Grand Master of the Golden-girdled Purple.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the honorary title of grand master of the golden-girdled purple.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，贈光祿大夫、秦州都督，陪葬乾陵。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-two, and was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Brightness and Military Commissioner of Qin Prefecture, with burial near Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously honored as grand master of splendid brightness and military commissioner of Qin Prefecture, and buried beside Qianling.

sentences.zh: 子曜，聖曆中，附會張易之，官正諫大夫。

translations.literal: His son Yao: during the Shengli era he attached himself to Zhang Yizhi and held the office of Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yao, in the Shengli period, joined Zhang Yizhi's faction and served as remonstrance grand master.

sentences.zh: 收從子 元敬元敬，隋選部郎邁之子，與收及收族兄德音齊名，世稱「河東三鳳」。

translations.literal: Shou's younger clansman cousin Yuanjing: Yuanjing, son of Mai, Lang of the Selection Department under the Sui, was famed alongside Shou and Shou's older clansman cousin Deyin; their age called them "the Three Phoenixes of Hedong."
translations.idiomatic: Shou's clansman Yuanjing, son of Mai, who had been a selection officer under the Sui, was as famous as Shou and Shou's elder clansman Deyin. Their generation called them the Three Phoenixes of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 收爲長離雛，德音爲鸑鷟，元敬年最少，爲鵷雛。

translations.literal: Shou was the young changli; Deyin was the juvenile zhuo; Yuanjing, youngest in years, was the young yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was likened to a young changli phoenix, Deyin to a young zhuo, and Yuanjing, the youngest of the three, to a young yuan.

sentences.zh: 武德中，爲秘書郎、天策府參軍，直記室、文學館學士。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he served as Secretary and Staff Officer of the Heavenly Stratagem Office, attending the Secretarial Office and as Scholar of the Literary Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude period he served as secretary, staff officer in the Heavenly Stratagem Office, attendant in the Secretarial Office, and scholar of the Literary Academy.

sentences.zh: 是時，收與房、杜處心腹之寄，更相結附。

translations.literal: At that time Shou and Fang and Du occupied positions of intimate trust and relied on one another in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shou, Fang, and Du stood in the Prince's inner circle and leaned on one another.

sentences.zh: 元敬謹畏，未嘗申款曲。

translations.literal: Yuanjing was cautious and wary and never opened himself in intimate friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was guarded and reserved and never offered easy intimacy.

sentences.zh: 如晦歎曰：「小記室不可得而親，不可得而疏！」

translations.literal: Ruhui sighed and said, "The young Secretarial Officer cannot be drawn close, yet cannot be kept at distance!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui sighed and said, "That young secretary—you cannot get close to him, yet you cannot keep him at arm's length either!"

sentences.zh: 秦王爲皇太子，除舍人。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin became Crown Prince, Yuanjing was appointed Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin became crown prince, Yuanjing was made attendant.

sentences.zh: 於是軍國之務總於東宮，而元敬掌文翰，號稱職。

translations.literal: Thereupon military and state affairs were gathered in the Eastern Palace, and Yuanjing handled documents—he was called well suited to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Military and civil affairs then centered on the Eastern Palace, and Yuanjing managed the documents—people said he filled the role.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 收孫 稷稷，字嗣通，道衡曾孫。

translations.literal: Shou's grandson Ji: Ji, styled Sitong, great-great-grandson of Daoheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's grandson Ji, styled Sitong, was the great-great-grandson of Daoheng.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the presented-scholar examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部郎中、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Lang of the Ministry of Rites and Drafting Secretary of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Ministry of Rites and the Central Secretariat, serving as lang and drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 與從祖兄曜更踐兩省，俱以辭章自名。

translations.literal: He and his older clansman cousin Yao in turn served in both secretariats, each making a name by literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He and his clansman Yao each served in turn in both secretariats, and both were known for their writing.

sentences.zh: 景龍末，爲諫議大夫、昭文館學士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jinglong era he was Remonstrating and Advising Grand Master and Scholar of the Zhaowen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Jinglong he was remonstrating and advising grand master and a scholar of the Zhaowen Academy.

sentences.zh: 初，貞觀、永徽間，虞世南、褚遂良以書顓家，後莫能繼。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Zhenguan and Yonghui, Yu Shinan and Chu Suiliang were preeminent in calligraphy; afterward none could succeed them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan and Yonghui, Yu Shinan and Chu Suiliang had dominated calligraphy; afterward no one matched them.

sentences.zh: 稷外祖魏征家多藏虞、褚書，故銳精臨仿，結體遒麗，遂以書名天下。

translations.literal: Ji's maternal grandfather Wei Zheng's house preserved many works by Yu and Chu; therefore Ji applied himself keenly to copying them, his structure forceful and elegant, and eventually his calligraphy was famed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's maternal grandfather Wei Zheng owned many works by Yu and Chu. Ji copied them with fierce devotion until his hand grew strong and graceful, and his calligraphy became famous under heaven.

sentences.zh: 畫又絶品。

translations.literal: His painting too was of supreme excellence.
translations.idiomatic: His painting, too, was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 睿宗在籓，喜之，以其子伯陽尚仙源公主。

translations.literal: When Ruizong was a princely heir, he favored Ji and had Ji's son Boyang marry Princess Xianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: While Ruizong was still a prince, he favored Ji and had Ji's son Boyang marry Princess Xianyuan.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，遷太常少卿，封晉國公，實封三百戸。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, Ji was transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, enfeoffed as Duke of Jin with three hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Ji became vice minister of ceremonies, was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin, and received three hundred households as his fief.

sentences.zh: 會鐘紹京爲中書令，稷諷使讓，因入言於帝曰：「紹京本胥史，無素才望，今特以勳進，師長百僚，恐非朝廷具瞻之美。」

translations.literal: When Zhong Shaojing was Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat, Ji urged him to yield the post and then entered to speak to the Emperor: "Shaojing was originally a clerk—he lacks established talent and reputation; now he advances solely by merit, to lead the hundred officials—I fear this is not the glory in which the court should be united in looking upward."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Shaojing was grand councilor, Ji prompted him to step down and then told the emperor, "Shaojing began as a petty clerk without long-standing talent or standing. To raise him now on merit alone to lead the hundred officials is hardly the sight the court should present to the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，遂許紹京讓，改戸部尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed, then permitted Shaojing to yield, and changed his appointment to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, allowed Shaojing to resign the post, and made him minister of revenue instead.

sentences.zh: 翌日，遷稷黃門侍郎，參知機務。

translations.literal: The next day Ji was transferred to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate to participate in deciding weighty affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ji was made vice minister of the Yellow Gate and given a share in deciding state affairs.

sentences.zh: 與崔日用數爭事帝前，罷爲左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He repeatedly disputed affairs with Cui Riyong before the Emperor and was dismissed to Left Regular Attendant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled repeatedly with Cui Riyong before the throne and was removed to left regular attendant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 歷太子少保、禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He served successively as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as junior tutor to the heir apparent and minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 帝以翊贊功，每召入宮中與決事，恩絶群臣。

translations.literal: The Emperor, for his service in supporting the succession, often summoned him into the palace to decide affairs with him—his favor surpassed all other ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his help in bringing Ruizong to the throne, the emperor often called him into the palace to decide matters with him, and his favor stood above all the rest.

sentences.zh: 竇懷貞誅，稷以知本謀，賜死萬年獄，年六十五。

translations.literal: When Dou Huaizhen was executed, Ji was condemned for knowing the original plot and was granted death in the prison of Wannian, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Huaizhen was put to death, Ji was judged to have known the plot from the start and was ordered to die in the prison at Wannian. He was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 稷子 伯陽伯陽爲駙馬都尉、安邑郡公，別食實封四百戸。

translations.literal: Ji's son Boyang: Boyang was Commandant of Escort Cavalry and Duke of Anyi Commandery, with a separate stipend of four hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Boyang was commandant of escort cavalry and Duke of Anyi, with an additional fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 稷死，坐貶晉州員外別駕，又流嶺表，自殺。

translations.literal: When Ji died, Boyang was punished by demotion to Supernumerary Assistant Prefect of Jin Prefecture, then exiled beyond the Ling Mountains, where he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji's death Boyang was demoted to supernumerary assistant prefect of Jin Prefecture, then banished south of the Ling range, where he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 伯陽子談，尚玄宗恒山公主，拜駙馬都尉、光祿員外卿。

translations.literal: Boyang's son Tan married Emperor Xuanzong's Princess Hengshan and was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry and Supernumerary Director of Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang's son Tan married Emperor Xuanzong's Princess Hengshan and was made commandant of escort cavalry and supernumerary director of splendid brightness.

sentences.zh: 馬周馬周，字賓王，博州茌平人。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou—Zhou was his name; his courtesy name was Binwang—a native of Chiping in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou, whose courtesy name was Binwang, was from Chiping in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，家窶狹。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his household was poor and cramped.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father early, and the family was poor and narrow in means.

sentences.zh: 嗜學，善《詩》、《春秋》。

translations.literal: He was avid for learning and skilled in the Odes and the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was accomplished in the Odes and the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 資曠邁，鄕人以無細謹，薄之。

translations.literal: His endowment was broad and unrestrained; fellow townsmen, because he lacked petty scrupulousness, held him in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was gifted with a broad, unbounded spirit, but his fellow townsfolk thought him careless in small matters and held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 武德中，補州助教，不治事。

translations.literal: In the Wude era, he was appointed assistant instructor of the prefecture and did not attend to his duties.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude reign, he was appointed assistant instructor in the prefecture but neglected his duties.

sentences.zh: 刺史達奚恕數咎讓，周乃去，客密州。

translations.literal: Prefect Daxi Shu repeatedly rebuked and reproached him; Zhou then left and lived as a guest in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Daxi Shu rebuked him again and again, so Ma Zhou departed and took lodging as a guest in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 趙仁本高其才，厚以裝，使入關。

translations.literal: Zhao Renben esteemed his talent, richly provisioned him for travel, and sent him to enter the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Renben admired his gifts, lavished travel provisions on him, and sent him toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 留客汴，爲浚儀令崔賢所辱，遂感激而西，舍新豐，逆旅主人不之顧，周命酒一斗八升，悠然獨酌，眾異之。

translations.literal: He lingered as a guest at Bian and was insulted by Cui Xian, magistrate of Junyi; stirred by indignation he went west, lodged at Xinfeng, and the innkeeper paid him no heed. Zhou ordered a peck and eight tenths of wine, drank alone with easy contentment—the onlookers all thought him strange.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped at Bian as a guest and was humiliated by Cui Xian, magistrate of Junyi. Stung to indignation, he traveled west and stopped at Xinfeng, where the innkeeper ignored him entirely. Ma Zhou ordered a peck and eight tenths of wine and drank alone with serene ease, to the wonder of all who saw him.

sentences.zh: 至長安，舍中郎將常何家。

translations.literal: Reaching Chang'an, he lodged at the home of Chang He, captain of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chang'an, he took lodging in the household of Chang He, captain of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，詔百官言得失。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan, an edict directed all officials to speak of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhenguan reign, the emperor decreed that all officials should speak on the empire's strengths and failings.

sentences.zh: 何武人，不涉學，周爲條二十餘事，皆當世所切。

translations.literal: He was a military man and unversed in learning; Zhou drafted for him more than twenty items, all pressing concerns of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Chang He was a soldier who had never touched scholarship; Ma Zhou drew up more than twenty items for him, each a matter urgently pressing upon the age.

sentences.zh: 太宗怪問何，何曰：「此非臣所能，家客馬周教臣言之。

translations.literal: Taizong asked in astonishment and questioned He, who said: "This is not within my own ability—it was my house guest Ma Zhou who taught me what to say.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong questioned Chang He in astonishment. He replied, "This is beyond what I could do alone—my house guest Ma Zhou taught me what to say.

sentences.zh: 客，忠孝人也。」

translations.literal: This guest is a man of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: That guest is a man of loyalty and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 帝即召之，間未至，遣使者四輩敦趣。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately summoned him; before he had arrived, he sent four sets of envoys in succession to urge him urgently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once summoned him, and before Ma Zhou had even arrived sent four successive envoys to press him onward.

sentences.zh: 及謁見，與語，帝大悅，詔直門下省。

translations.literal: When he was received in audience and the Emperor spoke with him, the Emperor was greatly pleased and decreed that he serve at the Secretariat gate.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience and the emperor spoke with him, the emperor was greatly pleased and ordered him stationed at the Secretariat gate.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜監察御史，奉使稱職。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Investigating Censor and, on missions entrusted to him, acquitted himself well.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed investigating censor and, on the missions entrusted to him, fulfilled his charge with distinction.

sentences.zh: 帝以何得人，賜帛三百段。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because He had obtained this man, bestowed three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering that Chang He had found a worthy man, rewarded him with three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 周上疏曰：

translations.literal: Zhou submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣每讀前史，見賢者忠孝事，未嘗不廢卷長想，思履其跡。

translations.literal: I, your servant, whenever I read the histories of former ages and see the deeds of loyalty and filial piety by worthy men, never fail to lay aside the scroll and muse long, thinking to follow in their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read the chronicles of former ages and encounter the loyal and filial deeds of worthy men, I cannot but set the scroll aside and dwell upon them at length, longing to walk in their footsteps.

sentences.zh: 臣不幸早失父母，犬馬之養，已無所施；

translations.literal: I, your servant, was unhappily deprived of my parents early; the nourishment owed to parents as to hounds and horses, I can no longer render.
translations.idiomatic: I was sadly bereft of my parents while still young, and can no longer offer them even the meanest care.

sentences.zh: 顧來事可爲者，惟忠義而已。

translations.literal: Yet in what remains to be done, there is only loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Of what lies ahead, only loyalty and righteousness remain for me to perform.

sentences.zh: 是以徒歩二千里，歸於陛下。

translations.literal: Therefore I walked two thousand li to come into Your Majesty's service.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason I walked two thousand li to place myself in Your Majesty's service.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以臣愚，擢臣不次。

translations.literal: Your Majesty did not count me foolish and promoted me out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty did not deem me unworthy and raised me beyond ordinary rank.

sentences.zh: 竊自惟念無以論報，輒竭區區，惟陛下所擇。

translations.literal: I secretly reflect that I have no means to repay this favor in kind and can only offer my humble utmost—let Your Majesty choose as you will.
translations.idiomatic: I can find no adequate way to repay such grace, and can only pour out what little I have—let Your Majesty take or leave it as you see fit.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見大安宮在宮城右，牆宇門闕，方紫極爲卑小。

translations.literal: I observe that Da'an Palace lies to the right within the palace city, yet its walls, gates, and towers are plainly mean beside the Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Da'an Palace stands to the right within the palace city, yet its walls, towers, and gates are plainly mean beside the Purple Forbidden.

sentences.zh: 東宮，皇太子居之，而在內；

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace, where the Crown Prince dwells, lies within;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace, where the crown prince dwells, lies within the inner precincts;

sentences.zh: 大安，至尊居之，反在外。

translations.literal: yet Da'an, where the Supreme One dwells, is set outside instead.
translations.idiomatic: yet Da'an Palace, where the supreme sovereign dwells, is set outside instead.

sentences.zh: 太上皇雖志清儉，愛惜人力，陛下不敢違，而蕃夷朝見，四方觀聽，有不足焉。

translations.literal: Though the Retired Emperor's mind is set on purity and frugality and on sparing human labor—and Your Majesty dare not disobey—when barbarians come to audience and all quarters look on, something is still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Though the retired emperor wishes to remain pure and frugal and to spare human labor—and Your Majesty dare not disobey—when foreign tribes come to audience and all the world looks on, something is still lacking.

sentences.zh: 臣願營雉堞門觀，務從高顯，以稱萬方之望，則大孝昭矣。

translations.literal: I wish that battlements, gates, and towers be built, striving for height and prominence to answer the hopes of all lands—then great filial piety would shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: I would have battlements, gates, and towers raised high and made conspicuous, to answer the hopes of all lands—then great filial piety would shine clear for all to see.

sentences.zh: 臣伏讀明詔，以二月幸九成宮。

translations.literal: I have read in reverence Your Majesty's clear edict that in the second month you will sojourn at Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Reading reverently Your Majesty's clear edict, I see that in the second month you will sojourn at Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 竊惟太上皇春秋高，陛下宜朝夕視膳。

translations.literal: I reflect that the Retired Emperor's years are advanced; Your Majesty ought to attend his meals morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the retired emperor's years are advanced, and Your Majesty ought to attend his meals morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 今所幸宮去京三百里而遠，非能旦發暮至也。

translations.literal: The palace you now favor lies three hundred li from the capital—hardly a place one can reach by dawn if one sets out at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: The palace you now favor lies three hundred li from the capital—not a distance one can cover between dawn and dusk.

sentences.zh: 萬有一太上皇思感，欲即見陛下，何以逮之？

translations.literal: If by any chance the Retired Emperor should be moved by longing and wish at once to see Your Majesty, how could that be quickly achieved?
translations.idiomatic: Should the retired emperor, moved by longing, wish at once to see Your Majesty, how could you reach him in time?

sentences.zh: 今茲本爲避暑行也，太上皇留熱處，而陛下走涼處，溫清之道，臣所未安。

translations.literal: This journey is meant for escaping the heat, yet the Retired Emperor remains where it is hot while Your Majesty hastens to where it is cool—the way of attending to a parent's warmth and comfort gives me no peace.
translations.idiomatic: This journey is meant to escape the heat, yet the retired emperor stays where it is hot while Your Majesty hastens to where it is cool—the proper care owed a parent in warmth and comfort leaves me deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 然詔書既下，業不中止，願示還期，以開眾惑。

translations.literal: Yet since the edict has already been issued and the undertaking cannot be halted, I ask that a date of return be announced to dispel the people's confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the edict has already gone forth and the journey cannot be called off—still, I ask that a date of return be announced, to lay the people's doubts to rest.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見詔宗室功臣悉就籓國，遂貽子孫，世守其政。

translations.literal: I observe that an edict directs all members of the imperial clan and meritorious ministers to take up their fiefdoms, granting them to their descendants to guard their offices generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: I observe the edict directing all imperial clansmen and meritorious ministers to take up their fiefdoms, granting them to their descendants to hold and govern in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 竊惟陛下之意，誠愛之重之，欲其裔緒承守，與國無疆也。

translations.literal: I reflect that Your Majesty's intent is truly to love and honor them, wishing their lineages to inherit and hold their posts, sharing boundless years with the state.
translations.idiomatic: I take Your Majesty's intent to be a true desire to love and honor them—to have their lineages inherit and hold fast, sharing unending years with the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣謂必如詔書者，陛下宜思所以安存之，富貴之，何必使世官也？

translations.literal: If matters must follow the edict as written, Your Majesty ought to consider how to keep them secure and prosper them—why must they hold hereditary office?
translations.idiomatic: If matters must follow the edict as written, Your Majesty ought rather to consider how to keep them secure and make them prosper—why must they hold hereditary office?

sentences.zh: 且堯、舜之父，有硃、均之子。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yao and Shun had worthy fathers, yet also sons in Zhu and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao and Shun had worthy fathers—and sons in Zhu and Jun besides.

sentences.zh: 若令有不肖子襲封嗣職，兆庶被殃，國家蒙患。

translations.literal: If unworthy sons were allowed to inherit fiefs and succeed to office, the myriad people would suffer calamity and the state would bear disaster.
translations.idiomatic: If unworthy sons were allowed to inherit fiefs and succeed to office, the myriad people would suffer and the state would bear the calamity.

sentences.zh: 正欲絶之，則子文之治猶在也；

translations.literal: When one wishes to cut a line off, Ziwen's good governance still stands as warning;
translations.idiomatic: When one wishes to cut a line off entirely, Ziwen's good governance still stands in memory;

sentences.zh: 正欲存之，則欒黶之惡已暴也。

translations.literal: when one wishes to preserve it, Luan Yan's wickedness is already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: when one wishes to preserve it, Luan Yan's wickedness already stands exposed to all.

sentences.zh: 必曰與其毒害於見存之人，甯割恩於已亡之臣，則向所謂愛之重之者，適所以傷之也。

translations.literal: If one must say, "Better to sever grace toward a dead minister than to let poison afflict the living," then what was called love and honor would in truth be what wounds them.
translations.idiomatic: If one must choose between letting poison afflict the living and cutting off the grace owed the dead, then what was called love and honor becomes, in truth, the very thing that destroys them.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜賦以茅土，疇以戸邑，必有材行，隨器而授。

translations.literal: I hold that they should be granted fiefs and allotted households and estates, and that only when talent and conduct are proven should office be conferred according to capacity.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that they should be granted fiefs and allotted households and estates, and that office should be conferred only where talent and conduct warrant it, each according to his measure.

sentences.zh: 雖幹翮非強，亦可以免累。

translations.literal: Even if their wings are not strong, they may yet be spared burden and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Even if their wings are not strong, they may yet be spared ruin and disgrace.

sentences.zh: 漢光武不任功臣以吏事，所以終全其世者，良得其術也。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han did not entrust meritorious ministers with administrative affairs; that he was able to preserve them to the end of their days shows he had mastered the right method indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han did not burden his meritorious ministers with administrative affairs—that he was able to preserve them to the end of their days shows he had mastered the right art indeed.

sentences.zh: 願陛下深思其事，使得奉大恩，而子孫終其福祿也。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would ponder this deeply, that they may receive great grace and their descendants enjoy their blessings and emoluments to the end.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty ponder this deeply, that they may receive your great grace and their descendants enjoy fortune and rank to the end of their days.

sentences.zh: 臣聞聖人之化天下，莫不以孝爲本，故曰：「孝莫大於嚴父，嚴父莫大於配天」，「國之大事，在祀與戎」，孔子亦言「吾不與祭，如不祭」，是聖人之重祭祀也。

translations.literal: I have heard that in the sage's transforming the realm, none fails to take filial piety as root. Hence it is said: "Of filial acts none is greater than honoring the father; of honoring the father none is greater than matching Heaven"; "The great affairs of state lie in sacrifice and war"; Confucius also said, "If I do not personally take part in the sacrifice, it is as though no sacrifice were held at all"—such is the sage's weight upon sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in transforming the realm, the sage takes filial piety as root. Hence the saying: "Of filial acts none is greater than honoring the father; of honoring the father none is greater than matching Heaven"; "The great affairs of state lie in sacrifice and war"; and Confucius said, "If I do not personally take part in the sacrifice, it is as though no sacrifice were held at all"—such is the weight the sage placed upon sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 自陛下踐祚，宗廟之享，未嘗親事。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, you have never personally attended the offerings at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, you have never personally attended the offerings at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 竊惟聖情，以乘輿一出，所費無蓺，故忍孝思，以便百姓。

translations.literal: I reflect that in Your Majesty's sage feeling, since a single departure of the imperial carriage costs without measure, you restrain filial longing to spare the people.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that in Your Majesty's sage heart, since even a single departure of the imperial carriage costs beyond reckoning, you restrain your filial longing to spare the people.

sentences.zh: 而一代史官，不書皇帝入廟，將何以貽厥孫謀、示來葉邪？

translations.literal: Yet if the historians of this age record no entry of the emperor into the temple, how will this be bequeathed to descendants' counsel or shown to generations yet to come?
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the historians of this age record no entry of the emperor into the temple, what counsel will this leave to your descendants, what example to generations yet unborn?

sentences.zh: 臣知大孝誠不在俎豆之間，然聖人訓人，必以己先之，示不忘本也。

translations.literal: I know that great filial piety truly lies not in sacrificial vessels alone, yet the sage in instructing others always goes first himself, showing that one must not forget one's roots.
