translations.idiomatic: I know that great filial piety is not truly measured by sacrificial vessels alone, yet the sage, in instructing others, always leads by his own example, showing that one must never forget one's roots.

sentences.zh: 臣聞致化之道，在求賢審官。

translations.literal: I have heard that the way to achieve transformation lies in seeking the worthy and scrutinizing office.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the way to bring about good order lies in seeking worthy men and scrutinizing appointments to office.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「惟名與器，不可以假人。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Names and regalia—these must not be lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Titles and the instruments of rank must not be lent to others.

sentences.zh: 是言慎舉之爲重也。

translations.literal: This is to say how weighty careful selection is.
translations.idiomatic: This speaks to how weighty careful selection truly is.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見王長通、白明達本樂工輿皁雜類；

translations.literal: I observe that Wang Changtong and Bai Mingda were originally musicians, carriage men, and sundry menials;
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Wang Changtong and Bai Mingda were originally musicians, grooms, and common menials;

sentences.zh: 韋般提、斛斯正無他材，獨解調馬。

translations.literal: Wei Bandi and Husi Zheng had no other talent and knew only how to train horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bandi and Husi Zheng had no other gifts—they knew only how to train horses.

sentences.zh: 雖術逾等夷，可厚賜金帛以富其家。

translations.literal: Though their skills surpass the common run, one might richly bestow gold and silk to enrich their households.
translations.idiomatic: Though their skills surpass the common run, they might richly be rewarded with gold and silk to enrich their households.

sentences.zh: 今超授高爵，與外廷朝會，騶豎倡子，鳴玉曳履，臣竊恥之。

translations.literal: Now they are promoted beyond measure to high rank and attend court alongside outer officials—grooms, jesters, and singing boys, jade chinking at their belts, skirts trailing—this I, your servant, secretly find shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have been promoted beyond measure to high rank and attend court alongside outer officials—grooms, jesters, and songboys, jade ornaments chiming at their belts, hems sweeping the floor—and I am secretly ashamed of it.

sentences.zh: 若朝命不可追改，尚宜不使在列，與士大夫爲伍。

translations.literal: If the court's appointments cannot be recalled and altered, at the least they ought not to stand in the ranks among grand masters and officials.
translations.idiomatic: If the court's appointments cannot be recalled, at the least they ought not to stand in the ranks alongside grand masters and officials.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，除侍御中。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and appointed him Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words and appointed him attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He spoke again, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He spoke again, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣歷觀夏、商、周、漢之有天下，傳祚相繼，多者八百餘年，少者猶四五百年，皆積德累業，恩結於人，豈無僻王，賴先哲以免。

translations.literal: I have examined in turn how Xia, Shang, Zhou, and Han held the realm: their lines passed the throne in succession—the longest enduring more than eight hundred years, the shortest still four or five hundred—all accumulating virtue and piling up merit, binding grace upon the people. Were there no wayward kings? Yet they were spared through the legacy of former sages.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying in turn how Xia, Shang, Zhou, and Han held the realm—the longest enduring more than eight hundred years, the shortest still four or five hundred, each dynasty heaping up virtue upon virtue and binding grace to the people—I see that though wayward kings arose, the legacy of former sages preserved them from ruin.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉逮周、隋，多者五六十年，少者三二十年而亡。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin down to Zhou and Sui, the longest lasted five or six decades, the shortest perished in two or three decades.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin down through Zhou and Sui, the longest endured five or six decades, the shortest perished in twenty or thirty years.

sentences.zh: 良由創業之君不務仁化，當時僅能自守，後無遺德可思，故傳嗣之主，其政少衰，一夫大呼，天下土崩矣。

translations.literal: This was truly because founding rulers did not pursue humane transformation; they could barely hold their gains in their own day, and left no lingering virtue for later ages to recall. Thus when succeeding heirs took the throne, governance soon declined—a single man cried out, and the realm collapsed like crumbling earth.
translations.idiomatic: This came chiefly because founding rulers did not pursue humane governance: they could barely hold what they had in their own day and left no lingering virtue for later ages to cherish. When their heirs succeeded, governance soon faltered—a single man cried out, and the realm collapsed like crumbling earth.

sentences.zh: 今陛下雖以大功定天下，而積德日淺，固當隆禹、湯、文、武之道，使恩有餘地，爲子孫立萬世之基，豈特持當年而已。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty has by great achievement settled the realm, accumulated virtue grows daily shallow. You ought rather to exalt the way of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, leaving grace with room to spare and laying a foundation for ten thousand generations—not merely holding fast to the present year alone.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty has by great merit settled the realm, the store of accumulated virtue grows daily shallow. You ought rather to exalt the way of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, leaving grace with room to spare and laying a foundation that will endure for ten thousand generations—not merely holding fast to the present day alone.

sentences.zh: 然自古明王聖主，雖因人設教，而大要節儉於身，恩加於人，故其下愛之如父母，仰之如日月，畏之如雷霆，卜祚遐長，而禍亂不作也。

translations.literal: Yet since antiquity sage kings and luminous sovereigns, though adapting teaching to men, took as their great principle frugality in their own persons and grace extended to others; hence their subjects loved them as parents, looked up to them as sun and moon, feared them as thunder—and their reigns endured long, and calamity and disorder did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since antiquity, even sage kings and luminous sovereigns, though they adapted their teaching to the men before them, made frugality in their own persons and grace extended to others their great principle; hence their subjects loved them as parents, looked up to them as sun and moon, feared them as thunder—and their reigns ran long, and calamity and disorder did not arise.

sentences.zh: 今百姓承喪亂之後，比於隋時才十分一，而徭役相望，兄去弟還，往來遠者五六千里，春秋冬夏，略無休時。

translations.literal: Today the people, in the wake of war and chaos, are scarcely one tenth what they were under Sui; yet corvée labor follows without pause—elder brother departs, younger brother returns—and those traveling back and forth from afar cover five or six thousand li, through spring, autumn, winter, and summer, with scarcely a moment of rest.
translations.idiomatic: Today the people, emerging from war and chaos, number scarcely one tenth what they did under the Sui; yet corvée assignments follow one upon another—one brother goes out, another returns—and those traveling from afar journey five or six thousand li through spring, summer, autumn, and winter with scarcely a moment of rest.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖詔減省，而有司不得廢作，徒行文書，役之如故。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty has decreed reductions, the responsible offices dare not halt their works and merely circulate documents—the levies continue as before.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty has decreed reductions, the responsible offices dare not halt their works and merely circulate documents—the levies continue as before.

sentences.zh: 四五年來，百姓頗嗟怨，以爲陛下不存養之。

translations.literal: Over the past four or five years the people have grown openly resentful, thinking that Your Majesty does not care for and nurture them.
translations.idiomatic: Over the past four or five years the people have grown openly resentful, believing that Your Majesty does not care for and nurture them.

sentences.zh: 堯之茅茨土階，禹之惡衣菲食，臣知不可復行於今。

translations.literal: Yao's thatched hut and earthen steps, Yu's coarse dress and meager fare—I know these cannot be practiced again today.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's thatched hut and earthen steps, Yu's coarse garments and meager fare—I know these cannot be practiced again in our age.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝惜百金之費而罷露臺，集上書囊以爲殿帷，所幸慎夫人衣不曳地；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han, sparing the cost of a hundred gold pieces, abandoned the Exposed Terrace; he gathered the satchels from memorials to make hall draperies, and Lady Shen, whom he favored, wore robes that did not trail on the ground;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han, sparing the hundred-gold cost of the Exposed Terrace, abandoned the project; he gathered the satchels from memorials to make hall draperies, and Lady Shen, whom he favored, wore robes that did not sweep the ground;

sentences.zh: 景帝亦以錦繡纂組妨害女功，特詔除之，所以百姓安樂。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing likewise held that brocade and ornamental stitching harmed women's work and specially decreed their prohibition—hence the people's peace and contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing likewise held that brocade and ornamental stitching wasted women's labor and specially decreed their abolition—hence the people's peace and contentment.

sentences.zh: 至孝武帝雖窮奢極侈，承文、景遺德，故人心不搖。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor Wu, though he exhausted wealth in extravagance, he inherited the lingering virtue of Wen and Jing, and so the people's hearts did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to Emperor Wu, though he exhausted the realm in extravagance, he still inherited the lingering virtue of Wen and Jing, and the people's hearts did not waver.

sentences.zh: 向使高祖之後即值武帝，天下必不能全。

translations.literal: Had the heirs of Gaozu immediately met with Emperor Wu, the realm could not have remained whole.
translations.idiomatic: Had Gaozu's heirs immediately succeeded to Emperor Wu's reign, the realm could not have remained whole.

sentences.zh: 此時代差近，事蹟可見。

translations.literal: This age is not far removed, and the traces of events may still be seen.
translations.idiomatic: That age is not far removed from our own, and the record stands plain before us.

sentences.zh: 今京師及益州諸處，營造供奉器物，並諸王妃主服飾，皆過靡麗。

translations.literal: Today in the capital and throughout the districts of Yizhou, objects made for imperial service and the robes and adornments of the princes' consorts and imperial princesses all exceed proper splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Today in the capital and throughout Yizhou, objects crafted for imperial service and the robes and adornments of princes' consorts and imperial princesses all exceed proper splendor.

sentences.zh: 臣聞昧旦丕顯，後世猶怠，作法於治，其弊猶亂。

translations.literal: I have heard that though one rises at dawn to achieve brilliance, later ages still grow lax; establish a pattern in time of order, and its corruption still breeds disorder.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that though one rises at dawn in pursuit of excellence, later ages still grow lax; establish custom in a time of order, and its decay will still breed disorder.

sentences.zh: 陛下少處人間，知百姓辛苦，前代成敗，目所親見，尚猶如此，而皇太子生長深宮，不更外事，即萬歲後，聖慮之所當憂也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty once lived among common men and know the people's hardship; the triumphs and failures of former ages you saw with your own eyes—yet things stand thus. How much more, when the crown prince, raised deep within the palace and knowing nothing of outward affairs, succeeds you—these are matters your sage concern ought dread.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once lived among common men and knows the people's hardship; the triumphs and failures of former ages you witnessed with your own eyes—yet things stand thus already. How much greater the matter for concern when the crown prince, raised deep within the palace and knowing nothing of the world outside, succeeds you in years to come.

sentences.zh: 臣竊尋自古黎庶怨叛，聚爲盜賊，其國無不即滅，人主雖悔，未有重能安全者。

translations.literal: I reflect that since antiquity, when the common people turn resentful and rebel, gathering as bandits, no state has failed to perish at once; though the ruler afterward repents, none has ever again secured safety.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that since antiquity, when the common people turn resentful and gather as bandits, no state has failed to perish at once; though the ruler afterward repents, none has ever secured safety again.

sentences.zh: 凡脩政教，當脩之於可脩之時。

translations.literal: In all repairing of governance and teaching, one must repair while repair is still possible.
translations.idiomatic: In all reform of governance and teaching, one must act while reform is still possible.

sentences.zh: 若事變一起而後悔之，無益也。

translations.literal: If one waits until troubles have already arisen and only then repents, it avails nothing.
translations.idiomatic: To wait until disaster has already struck and only then repent avails nothing.

sentences.zh: 故人主每見前代之亡，則知其政教之所由喪，而不知其身之失。

translations.literal: Hence rulers, whenever they see the fall of a former age, know through what failure of governance and teaching it was lost, yet do not know their own errors.
translations.idiomatic: Hence rulers, whenever they witness the fall of a former age, know through what failure of governance and teaching it was lost—yet cannot see their own errors.

sentences.zh: 故紂笑桀之亡，而幽、厲笑紂之亡，隋煬帝又笑齊、魏之失國也。

translations.literal: Thus Zhou of Shang laughed at Jie of Xia's ruin; You and Li laughed at Zhou's ruin; and Emperor Yang of Sui laughed at Qi and Wei's loss of state.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhou of Shang laughed at Jie of Xia's ruin; Kings You and Li of Zhou laughed at Zhou of Shang's fall; and Emperor Yang of Sui laughed at Qi and Wei's loss of their realms.

sentences.zh: 今之視煬帝，猶煬帝之視齊、魏也。

translations.literal: Those who look upon Yang today are as Yang looked upon Qi and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Those who look upon Emperor Yang today stand where Emperor Yang himself stood when he looked upon Qi and Wei.

sentences.zh: 往貞觀初，率土荒儉，一匹絹才易斗米，而天下帖然者，百姓知陛下憂憐之，故人人自安無謗讟也。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan years, the realm within the four seas was stricken with famine—a bolt of silk scarcely fetched a peck of grain—yet the empire remained tranquil because the people knew Your Majesty grieved for and pitied them; each man rested secure and there was no complaint.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years famine gripped the land—a bolt of silk scarcely bought a peck of grain—yet the empire remained tranquil because the people knew Your Majesty grieved for and pitied them; each man rested secure, and there was no outcry of complaint.

sentences.zh: 五六年來，頻歲豐稔，一匹絹易粟十餘斛，而百姓咸怨，以爲陛下不憂憐之。

translations.literal: Over the past five or six years harvests have been abundant year after year—a bolt of silk buys more than ten hu of grain—yet the people all complain, thinking Your Majesty does not grieve for and pity them.
translations.idiomatic: Over the past five or six years harvests have run abundant—a bolt of silk buys more than ten hu of grain—yet the people all complain, believing that Your Majesty no longer grieves for and pities them.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 今營爲者，多不急之務故也。

translations.literal: Because what is now undertaken is mostly unneeded business.
translations.idiomatic: Because what is now undertaken is mostly business of no urgent need.

sentences.zh: 自古以來，國之興亡，不由積畜多少，在百姓苦樂也。

translations.literal: Since antiquity the rise and fall of states has not depended on how much was stored up, but on whether the people suffered or were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity the rise and fall of states has never depended on the size of the treasury, but on whether the people suffered or prospered.

sentences.zh: 且以近事驗之，隋貯洛口倉而李密因之，積布帛東都而王世充據之，西京府庫亦爲國家之用。

translations.literal: Test this by recent events: Sui stored grain at the Luokou granary and Li Mi seized upon it; it piled cloth and silk at the eastern capital and Wang Shichong took possession; the western capital's treasuries likewise became spoils for the contending powers.
translations.idiomatic: Judge by recent events: the Sui stored grain at the Luokou granary and Li Mi seized upon it; it piled cloth and silk at the eastern capital and Wang Shichong took possession; the western capital's treasuries likewise became spoils for rebels and usurpers.

sentences.zh: 向使洛口、東都無粟帛，王世充、李密未能必聚大眾。

translations.literal: Had Luokou and the eastern capital held no grain or silk, Wang Shichong and Li Mi could not so readily have gathered great hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Had Luokou and the eastern capital held no grain or silk, Wang Shichong and Li Mi could not so readily have gathered great hosts.

sentences.zh: 但貯積者，固有國之常，要當人有餘力而後收之，豈人勞而強斂之以資寇邪？

translations.literal: Storage is indeed the constant practice of statecraft, yet one ought collect only after the people have strength to spare—how can one levy harshly while they toil and thereby provision raiders?
translations.idiomatic: To store up reserves is indeed the constant practice of statecraft—but one ought collect only when the people have strength to spare. How can one levy harshly while they toil and thereby arm one's enemies?

sentences.zh: 夫儉以息人，貞觀初，陛下己躬爲之，今行之不難也。

translations.literal: Frugality to give the people rest—in early Zhenguan Your Majesty already practiced this yourself; to practice it now would not be hard.
translations.idiomatic: Frugality to give the people rest—in early Zhenguan Your Majesty already practiced this yourself; to practice it now would not be hard.

sentences.zh: 爲之一日，則天下知之，式歌且舞矣。

translations.literal: Practice it for a single day and the realm will know it—they will sing and dance in joy.
translations.idiomatic: Practice it for a single day and the realm will know it—the people will sing and dance in joy.

sentences.zh: 若人既勞，而周之不息，萬一中國水旱，而邊方有風塵之警，狂狡竊發，非徒旰食晏寢而已。

translations.literal: If the people are already exhausted and the corvée does not cease, then should the central provinces suffer flood or drought while the frontier raises alarms of war, and the violent and cunning steal forth to rise—all this would mean more than merely skipping meals and forgoing sleep.
translations.idiomatic: If the people are already exhausted and the levies do not cease, then should the heartland suffer flood or drought while the frontier raises alarms of war, and the violent and cunning rise in rebellion—the danger would be far graver than merely losing sleep and skipping meals.

sentences.zh: 古語云：「動人以行不以言，應天以實不以文。」

translations.literal: An old saying runs: "Move men by deeds, not words; respond to Heaven with substance, not ornament.
translations.idiomatic: An old saying runs, "Move men by deeds, not words; respond to Heaven with substance, not ornament.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之明，誠欲厲精爲政，不煩遠采上古，但及貞觀初，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's luminous understanding, if you truly wish to sharpen your spirit in governance, there is no need to reach far back to high antiquity—only return to early Zhenguan, and the realm would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's luminous understanding, if you truly wish to sharpen your spirit in governance, there is no need to reach back to high antiquity—only return to early Zhenguan, and the realm would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 昔賈誼謂漢文帝云「可痛哭及長歎息者」，言：「當韓信王楚、彭越王梁、英布王淮南之時，使文帝即天子位，必不能安。」

translations.literal: In former times Jia Yi said to Emperor Wen of Han of matters "that could make one weep aloud and sigh deeply," saying: "When Han Xin was king of Chu, Peng Yue king of Liang, and Ying Bu king of Huainan—had Wen immediately ascended the throne, he could not have remained secure."
translations.idiomatic: In former times Jia Yi told Emperor Wen of Han of matters "that could make one weep aloud and sigh deeply," saying, "When Han Xin held Chu, Peng Yue held Liang, and Ying Bu held Huainan—had Wen immediately ascended the throne, he could not have remained secure."

sentences.zh: 又言：「賴諸王年少，傅相制之，長大之後，必生禍亂。」

translations.literal: He also said: "They were spared only because the princes were still young and tutors and ministers restrained them—but once grown, calamity and disorder would surely arise."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "They were spared only because the princes were still young and tutors and ministers restrained them—but once grown, calamity and disorder would surely arise."

sentences.zh: 後世皆以誼言爲是。

translations.literal: Later ages have all held Jia Yi's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages have all held Jia Yi's words to be true.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀今諸將功臣，陛下所與定天下，無威略振主如韓、彭者；

translations.literal: I observe that among the generals and meritorious ministers who fixed the realm with Your Majesty, none possesses such dread power and stratagem to shake the sovereign as Han and Peng did;
translations.idiomatic: I observe that among the generals and meritorious ministers who fixed the realm with Your Majesty, none possesses such terrifying power and stratagem as Han and Peng did, such as might shake the throne;

sentences.zh: 而諸王年並幼少，縱其長大，陛下之日，必無他心，然則萬代之後，不可不慮。

translations.literal: Yet all the princes are still young; even when grown, so long as Your Majesty lives they will surely harbor no other intent—yet for ten thousand generations hence, this cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all the princes are still young; even when grown, so long as Your Majesty lives they will surely harbor no other intent—yet for ten thousand generations to come, this cannot go unconsidered.

sentences.zh: 漢、晉以來，亂天下者，何嘗不在諸王。

translations.literal: Since Han and Jin, has turmoil of the realm ever come from anywhere but the princes?
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Jin, has the realm ever been thrown into chaos by anyone other than the princes?

sentences.zh: 皆由樹置失宜，不豫爲節制，以至滅亡。

translations.literal: All because they were planted and established improperly, with no forethought of restraint, until ruin followed.
translations.idiomatic: All because they were established in the wrong measure, with no restraint laid down in advance, until ruin followed.

sentences.zh: 人主豈不知其然，溺於私愛爾。

translations.literal: Do rulers not know this? They are drowned in private affection, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Do rulers not know this? They are drowned in private affection—that is all.

sentences.zh: 故前車既覆，而後車不改轍也。

translations.literal: Hence the cart ahead overturns, yet the cart behind does not change course.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the cart ahead overturns, yet the cart behind does not change its track.

sentences.zh: 今天下百姓尚少，而諸王已多，其寵遇過厚者，臣愚慮之，非特恃恩驕矜也。

translations.literal: Today the people of the realm are still few, yet the princes are already many; those excessively favored—I fear, in my foolish view—will not merely grow arrogant on imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Today the people of the realm are still few, yet the princes are already many; those who receive excessive favor—I fear, in my foolish view—will not merely grow arrogant on imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 昔魏武帝寵陳思王，文帝即位，防守禁閉同獄囚焉。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Wu of Wei favored Prince Si of Chen; when Emperor Wen succeeded, he was guarded and confined like a prisoner in a dungeon.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Emperor Wu of Wei favored Prince Si of Chen; when Emperor Wen succeeded, he was guarded and confined like a prisoner in a dungeon.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why was this?
translations.idiomatic: Why was this?

sentences.zh: 先帝加恩太多，故嗣主疑而畏之也。

translations.literal: The former emperor had bestowed too much favor, so the succeeding sovereign suspected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor had bestowed too much favor, so the succeeding sovereign suspected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 此武帝寵陳思王，適所以苦之也。

translations.literal: Thus in favoring Prince Si of Chen, Emperor Wu had only brought him suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in favoring Prince Si of Chen, Emperor Wu had only brought him suffering.

sentences.zh: 且帝子身食大國，何患不富，而歲別優賜，曾無限極。

translations.literal: Moreover, an emperor's son feeds upon a great fief—what need has he to fear poverty? Yet year after year special grants are made, without limit or end.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, an emperor's son feeds upon a great fief—what need has he to fear poverty? Yet year after year special grants are made, without limit or end.

sentences.zh: 里語曰：「貧不學儉，富不學奢。」

translations.literal: A village saying runs: "The poor do not need to learn thrift; the rich do not need to learn extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: A village saying runs, "The poor do not need to learn thrift; the rich do not need to learn extravagance.

sentences.zh: 言自然也。

translations.literal: This speaks to what is natural."
translations.idiomatic: This speaks to what is natural.

sentences.zh: 今大聖創業，豈唯處置見子弟而已，當制長久之法，使萬代奉行。

translations.literal: Now the Great Sage has founded the enterprise—surely this is not merely a matter of arranging his sons and younger brothers; he ought to establish lasting law that ten thousand generations may follow.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Great Sage has founded the enterprise—surely this is not merely a matter of arranging his sons and younger brothers; he ought to establish lasting law that ten thousand generations may follow.

sentences.zh: 臣聞天下者以人爲本。

translations.literal: I have heard that the realm takes the people as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the realm takes the people as its foundation.

sentences.zh: 必也使百姓安樂，在刺史、縣令爾。

translations.literal: Surely to make the common people secure and at ease lies with the prefectural inspectors and county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Surely to make the common people secure and at ease lies with the prefectural inspectors and county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 縣令既眾，不可皆賢，但州得良刺史可矣。

translations.literal: Magistrates are many and cannot all be worthy—but if each province finds a good inspector, that suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates are many and cannot all be worthy—but if each province finds a good inspector, that suffices.

sentences.zh: 天下刺史得人，陛下端拱岩廊之上，夫復何爲？

translations.literal: If the empire's inspectors are well chosen, what need has Your Majesty to do anything, seated in dignity upon the lofty hall?
translations.idiomatic: If the empire's inspectors are well chosen, what need has Your Majesty to do anything, seated in dignity upon the lofty hall?

sentences.zh: 古者郡守、縣令皆選賢德，欲有所用，必先試以臨人，或由二千石高第入爲宰相。

translations.literal: In antiquity, prefects and magistrates were all chosen for virtue and talent; when one was to be employed, he was first tested in governing men, or might enter the chancellorship through high standing among the two-thousand-bushel officials.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, prefects and magistrates were all chosen for virtue and talent; when one was to be employed, he was first tested in governing men, or might enter the chancellorship through high standing among the two-thousand-bushel officials.

sentences.zh: 今獨重內官，縣令、刺史頗輕其選。

translations.literal: Today inner court officials alone are heavily esteemed, while the selection of magistrates and inspectors is rather slighted.
translations.idiomatic: Today inner court officials alone are heavily esteemed, while the selection of magistrates and inspectors is rather slighted.

sentences.zh: 又刺史多武夫勳人，或京官不稱職始出補外；

translations.literal: Moreover, most inspectors are military men and men of merit—or capital officials who proved unfit for their posts are sent out to fill outer appointments;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, most inspectors are military men and men of merit—or capital officials who proved unfit for their posts are sent out to fill outer appointments;

sentences.zh: 折沖果毅身力強者入爲中郎將，其次乃補邊州。

translations.literal: Those strongest in repelling enemies and resolute in combat enter as commandants of the palace guard; only the next rank are assigned to frontier provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Those strongest in repelling enemies and resolute in combat enter as commandants of the palace guard; only the next rank are assigned to frontier provinces.

sentences.zh: 而以德行才術擢者，十不能一。

translations.literal: Of those promoted for virtue, conduct, talent, and skill, not one in ten can be found.
translations.idiomatic: Of those promoted for virtue, conduct, talent, and skill, not one in ten can be found.

sentences.zh: 所以百姓未安，殆在於此。

translations.literal: That the people are not yet at ease lies, I suspect, in this.
translations.idiomatic: That the people are not yet at ease lies, I suspect, in this.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝稱善。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised it.

sentences.zh: 擢拜給事中，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou was promoted to Gentleman Attendant-at-Discussions and then transferred to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou was promoted to Gentleman Attendant-at-Discussions and then transferred to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周善敷奏，機辯明銳，動中事會，裁處周密，時譽歸之。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou excelled at laying out memorials: quick and sharp in debate, always striking the crux of affairs, thorough in deciding and disposing—and the acclaim of the age flowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou excelled at laying out memorials: quick and sharp in debate, always striking the crux of affairs, thorough in deciding and disposing—and the acclaim of the age flowed to him.

sentences.zh: 帝每曰：「我暫不見周即思之。」

translations.literal: The emperor often said, "Briefly away from Zhou, I already miss him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said, "Briefly away from Ma Zhou, I already miss him.

sentences.zh: 岑文本謂所親曰：「馬君論事，會文切理，無一言可損益，聽之纚纚，令人忘倦。

translations.literal: Cen Text told those close to him, "When Master Ma discusses affairs, his language meets the text and cuts to principle—not a word can be added or taken away; listening to him, the flow never wearies one.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Text told those close to him, "When Master Ma discusses affairs, his language meets the text and cuts to principle—not a word can be added or taken away; listening to him, the flow never wearies one.

sentences.zh: 蘇、張、終、賈正應此耳。

translations.literal: Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Zhong Jun, and Jia Yi were truly men of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Zhong Jun, and Jia Yi were truly men of this kind.

sentences.zh: 然鳶肩火色，騰上必速，恐不能久。」

translations.literal: Yet his shoulders are like a kite's and his complexion fire-red—those who rise swiftly cannot long endure, I fear."
translations.idiomatic: Yet his shoulders are like a kite's and his complexion fire-red—those who rise swiftly cannot long endure, I fear."

sentences.zh: 俄遷治書侍御史，兼知諫議大夫，檢校晉王府長史。

translations.literal: Not long after he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Censorate, concurrently acting as remonstrance counsellor, and made acting chief administrator of the Prince of Jin's household.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Censorate, concurrently acting as remonstrance counsellor, and made acting chief administrator of the Prince of Jin's household.

sentences.zh: 王爲皇太子，拜中書侍郎，兼太子右庶子。

translations.literal: When the prince became crown prince, Ma Zhou was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, concurrently right assistant to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Ma Zhou was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, concurrently right assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷中書令，猶兼庶子。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, still concurrently assistant to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, still concurrently assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時置太子司議郎，帝高其除。

translations.literal: At that time the office of remonstrance adviser to the crown prince was established, and the emperor held his appointment in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the office of remonstrance adviser to the crown prince was established, and the emperor held Ma Zhou's appointment in high regard.

sentences.zh: 周歎曰：「恨吾資品妄高，不得歷此官。」

translations.literal: Ma Zhou sighed and said, "I regret that my qualifications were unduly elevated—I was not able to hold this office myself.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou sighed and said, "I regret that my qualifications were unduly elevated—I was not able to hold this office myself.

sentences.zh: 帝征遼，留輔太子定州。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Liaodong, Ma Zhou was left behind at Dingzhou to assist the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Liaodong, Ma Zhou was left behind at Dingzhou to assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及還，攝吏部尚書，進銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Upon the emperor's return, he served as acting Minister of Personnel and was advanced to Grand Master with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Upon the emperor's return, he served as acting Minister of Personnel and was advanced to Grand Master with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以飛白書賜周曰：「鸞鳳沖霄，必假羽翼；

translations.literal: The emperor once wrote in flying-white script and bestowed it upon Ma Zhou, saying, "The luan and phoenix soar to the sky—they must borrow wings;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wrote in flying-white script and bestowed it upon Ma Zhou, saying, "The luan and phoenix soar to the sky—they must borrow wings;

sentences.zh: 股肱之寄，要在忠力。」

translations.literal: the charge laid upon my arms and thighs lies above all in loyalty and strength."
translations.idiomatic: the charge laid upon my arms and thighs lies above all in loyalty and strength."

sentences.zh: 周病消渴連年，帝幸翠微宮，求勝地爲構第，每詔尚書食具膳，上醫使者視護，躬爲調藥，太子問疾。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou suffered from wasting thirst for years; the emperor visited the Cuiwei Palace, sought a fine site to build him a mansion, repeatedly ordered the Ministry of Revenues to supply full meals, sent the finest physicians to attend him, personally mixed medicines for him, and the crown prince inquired after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou suffered from wasting thirst for years; the emperor visited the Cuiwei Palace, sought a fine site to build him a mansion, repeatedly ordered the Ministry of Revenues to supply full meals, sent the finest physicians to attend him, personally mixed medicines for him, and the crown prince inquired after his illness.

sentences.zh: 疾甚，周取所上章奏悉焚之，曰：「管、晏暴君之過，取身後名，吾不爲也！」

translations.literal: When his illness grew severe, Ma Zhou took all the memorials he had submitted and burned them, saying, "Guan Zhong and Yan Ying reproached their rulers' failings to win fame after death—I will not do this!
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew severe, Ma Zhou took all the memorials he had submitted and burned them, saying, "Guan Zhong and Yan Ying reproached their rulers' failings to win fame after death—I will not do this!

sentences.zh: 二十二年卒，年四十八，贈幽州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died, aged forty-eight; he was posthumously made regional commander of Youzhou and buried beside the Zhaoling tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he died, aged forty-eight; he was posthumously made regional commander of Youzhou and buried beside the Zhaoling tomb.

sentences.zh: 初，帝遇周厚，周頗自負。

translations.literal: At first the emperor treated Ma Zhou with great favor, and Ma Zhou grew rather self-assured.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor treated Ma Zhou with great favor, and Ma Zhou grew rather self-assured.

sentences.zh: 爲御史時，遣人以圖購宅，眾以其興書生，素無貲，皆竊笑。

translations.literal: While serving as censor he sent men with a blueprint to buy a house; the crowd, knowing him for a penniless scholar risen from nothing, all secretly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as censor he sent men with a blueprint to buy a house; the crowd, knowing him for a penniless scholar risen from nothing, all secretly laughed.

sentences.zh: 它日，白有佳宅，直二百萬，周遽以聞，詔有司給直，並賜奴婢什物，由是人乃悟。

translations.literal: Another day he was told of a fine house worth two million cash; Ma Zhou immediately reported it, and an edict ordered the offices to pay the price and also bestowed slaves, maids, and furnishings—whereupon people understood.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he was told of a fine house worth two million cash; Ma Zhou immediately reported it, and an edict ordered the offices to pay the price and also bestowed slaves, maids, and furnishings—whereupon people understood.

sentences.zh: 周每行郡縣，食必進雞，小吏訟之。

translations.literal: Whenever Ma Zhou traveled through commanderies and counties, chicken was invariably served at meals; a petty clerk sued him over it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Ma Zhou traveled through commanderies and counties, chicken was invariably served at meals; a petty clerk sued him over it.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我禁御史食肉，恐州縣廣費，食雞尚何與？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I forbade censors from eating meat for fear counties and prefectures would expend lavishly—what has chicken to do with this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I forbade censors from eating meat for fear counties and prefectures would expend lavishly—what has chicken to do with this?

sentences.zh: 榜吏斥之。

translations.literal: He had the clerk beaten and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: He had the clerk beaten and driven off.

sentences.zh: 及領選，猶廢浚儀令。

translations.literal: When he took charge of selections, he still abolished the post of magistrate of Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: When he took charge of selections, he still abolished the post of magistrate of Junyi.

sentences.zh: 先是，京師晨暮傳呼以警眾，後置鼓代之，俗曰「冬冬鼓」；

translations.literal: Before this, the capital at dawn and dusk used call-and-response to warn the populace; afterward drums were installed in place of this—the people called them the "dong-dong drums";
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the capital at dawn and dusk used call-and-response to warn the populace; afterward drums were installed in place of this—the people called them the "dong-dong drums";

sentences.zh: 品官舊服止黃紫，於是三品服紫，四品五品硃，六品七品綠，八品九品青；

translations.literal: Officials of rank had formerly worn only yellow and purple; then third rank wore purple, fourth and fifth cinnabar, sixth and seventh green, eighth and ninth blue-green;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of rank had formerly worn only yellow and purple; then third rank wore purple, fourth and fifth cinnabar, sixth and seventh green, eighth and ninth blue-green;

sentences.zh: 城門入由左，出由右；

translations.literal: city gates: enter by the left, exit by the right;
translations.idiomatic: city gates: enter by the left, exit by the right;

sentences.zh: 飛驛以達警急；

translations.literal: flying courier stations to convey urgent alarms;
translations.idiomatic: flying courier stations to convey urgent alarms;

sentences.zh: 納居人地租；

translations.literal: collecting ground rent from residents;
translations.idiomatic: collecting ground rent from residents;

sentences.zh: 宿衞大小番直；

translations.literal: palace guards of all ranks on rotating watch;
translations.idiomatic: palace guards of all ranks on rotating watch;

sentences.zh: 截驛馬尾；

translations.literal: trimming courier horses' tails;
translations.idiomatic: trimming courier horses' tails;

sentences.zh: 城門、衞舍、守捉士，月散配諸縣，各取一，以防其過；

translations.literal: gate guards, guard barracks, and garrison soldiers—each month one from each was assigned among the counties to prevent misconduct;
translations.idiomatic: gate guards, guard barracks, and garrison soldiers—each month one from each was assigned among the counties to prevent misconduct;

sentences.zh: 皆周建白。

translations.literal: all these were Ma Zhou's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: all these were Ma Zhou's proposals.

sentences.zh: 自周亡，帝思之甚，將假方士術求見其儀形。

translations.literal: After Ma Zhou's death the emperor missed him deeply and intended to employ alchemical arts to see his likeness.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Zhou's death the emperor missed him deeply and intended to employ alchemical arts to see his likeness.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，追贈尚書右僕射、高唐縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended, Ma Zhou was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Gaotang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended, Ma Zhou was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Gaotang County.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，配享高宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era he was enshrined in the hall of Emperor Gaozong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuigong era he was enshrined in the hall of Emperor Gaozong's temple.

sentences.zh: 周子 載子載，咸亨中爲司列少常伯，與裴行儉分掌選事，言吏部者稱裴、馬焉。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou's son Ma Zai, courtesy name Zizai—in the Xianheng era served as vice minister of the Secretariat for ranking, shared charge of appointments with Pei Xingjian, and those who spoke of the Ministry of Personnel named Pei and Ma.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou's son Ma Zai, courtesy name Zizai—in the Xianheng era served as vice minister of the Secretariat for ranking, shared charge of appointments with Pei Xingjian, and those who spoke of the Ministry of Personnel named Pei and Ma.

sentences.zh: 終雍州長史。

translations.literal: He ended as chief administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as chief administrator of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：周之遇太宗，顧不異哉！

translations.literal: The encomium says: Was Ma Zhou's meeting with Emperor Taizong not singular indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Was Ma Zhou's meeting with Emperor Taizong not singular indeed!

sentences.zh: 由一介草茅言天下事，若素宦於朝、明習憲章者，非王佐才，疇以及茲？

translations.literal: From a single blade of thatch in the fields to speak of the empire's affairs as though he had always served at court and knew the statutes by heart—had he not possessed talent fit to assist a king, who could have reached this?
translations.idiomatic: From a single blade of thatch in the fields to speak of the empire's affairs as though he had always served at court and knew the statutes by heart—had he not possessed talent fit to assist a king, who could have reached this?

sentences.zh: 其自視與築岩、釣渭亦何以異！

translations.literal: How was his view of himself different from building on a cliff or fishing beside the Wei!
translations.idiomatic: How was his view of himself different from building on a cliff or fishing beside the Wei!

sentences.zh: 跡夫帝銳於立事，而周所建皆切一時，以明佐聖，故君宰間不膠漆而固，恨相得晩，宜矣。

translations.literal: Mark how the emperor was keen to establish affairs, and all Ma Zhou proposed was urgent to the moment; with a clear man assisting a sage, lord and minister needed no glue or lacquer to bind firm—regret that they found each other late was only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Mark how the emperor was keen to establish affairs, and all Ma Zhou proposed was urgent to the moment; with a clear man assisting a sage, lord and minister needed no glue or lacquer to bind firm—regret that they found each other late was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 然周才不逮傅説、呂望，使後世未有述焉，惜乎！

translations.literal: Yet Ma Zhou's talent did not reach Fu Yue or Lü Wang—and that later ages have no full account of him is a pity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ma Zhou's talent did not reach Fu Yue or Lü Wang—and that later ages have no full account of him is a pity!

sentences.zh: 韋挺韋挺，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Ting—Ting was his name—a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父沖，仕隋爲民部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Chong served the Sui as Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong served the Sui as Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 挺少與隱太子善，高祖平京師，署隴西公府祭酒。

translations.literal: In youth Wei Ting was on good terms with the Hidden Crown Prince; when Emperor Gaozu pacified the capital, he was appointed libationer of the Duke of Longxi's household.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Wei Ting was on good terms with the Hidden Crown Prince; when Emperor Gaozu pacified the capital, he was appointed libationer of the Duke of Longxi's household.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子左衞驃騎，檢校左衞率。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to commander of the Left Guard Wing of Cavalry in the crown prince's household, and acting commander of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to commander of the Left Guard Wing of Cavalry in the crown prince's household, and acting commander of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 太子遇之厚，宮臣無與比。

translations.literal: The crown prince treated him generously—among palace officials none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince treated him generously—among palace officials none could compare.

sentences.zh: 武德七年，帝避暑仁智宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wude the emperor spent the summer at Renzhi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wude the emperor spent the summer at Renzhi Palace.

sentences.zh: 或言太子與宮臣謀逆，又慶州刺史楊文幹坐大逆誅，辭連東宮，帝專責宮臣，由是挺與杜淹、王珪等皆流越巂。

translations.literal: Some said the crown prince and palace officials plotted rebellion; moreover Yang Wengan, prefect of Qingzhou, was executed for great treason and implicated the Eastern Palace in his confession—the emperor blamed the palace officials exclusively, and for this Wei Ting, Du Yan, Wang Gui, and others were all exiled to Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: Some said the crown prince and palace officials plotted rebellion; moreover Yang Wengan, prefect of Qingzhou, was executed for great treason and implicated the Eastern Palace in his confession—the emperor blamed the palace officials exclusively, and for this Wei Ting, Du Yan, Wang Gui, and others were all exiled to Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召拜主爵郎中。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled and appointed director of the Bureau of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled and appointed director of the Bureau of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，王珪數薦之，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Wang Gui repeatedly recommended him, and he was transferred to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Wang Gui repeatedly recommended him, and he was transferred to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部、黃門侍郎，拜御史大夫、扶陽縣男。

translations.literal: He passed through the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Director of the Department of the Imperial Household, and was appointed Censor-in-Chief and Baron of Fuyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Director of the Department of the Imperial Household, and was appointed Censor-in-Chief and Baron of Fuyang County.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂挺曰：「卿之任大夫，獨朕意，左右無爲卿地者！」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to Wei Ting, "In appointing you Censor-in-Chief, only my own intent decided it—none at my side made room for you!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said to Wei Ting, "In appointing you Censor-in-Chief, only my own intent decided it—none at my side made room for you!

sentences.zh: 挺曰：「臣駑下，不足以辱高位，且非勳非舊，而在籓邸故僚上，願後臣以勸立功者。」

translations.literal: Wei Ting said, "I, your servant, am slow and base—not worthy to disgrace so high a post; moreover I neither earned merit nor am an old companion, yet I stand above former colleagues of Your Majesty's princely household; I would ask that you place me after others, to encourage those who have achieved merit."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting said, "I, your servant, am slow and base—not worthy to disgrace so high a post; moreover I neither earned merit nor am an old companion, yet I stand above former colleagues of Your Majesty's princely household; I would ask that you place me after others, to encourage those who have achieved merit."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 是時承隋大亂，風俗薄惡，人不知教。

translations.literal: At that time, inheriting the great disorder of the Sui, customs were shallow and corrupt, and men knew nothing of teaching.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, inheriting the great disorder of the Sui, customs were shallow and corrupt, and men knew nothing of teaching.

sentences.zh: 挺上疏曰：「父母之恩，昊天罔極；

translations.literal: Wei Ting submitted a memorial, saying, "The grace of parents—boundless as heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting submitted a memorial, saying, "The grace of parents—boundless as heaven;

sentences.zh: 創巨之痛，終身何已。

translations.literal: the pain of deepest wound—when can it ever end in a lifetime?
translations.idiomatic: the pain of deepest wound—when can it ever end in a lifetime?

sentences.zh: 今衣冠士族，辰日不哭，謂爲重喪，親賓來吊，輒不臨舉。

translations.literal: Today among gentry clans, on chen days they do not weep, calling it a doubly heavy mourning; when kin and guests come to condole, they do not even attend the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Today among gentry clans, on chen days they do not weep, calling it a doubly heavy mourning; when kin and guests come to condole, they do not even attend the rites.

sentences.zh: 又閭里細人，每有重喪，不即發問，先造邑社，待營辦具，乃始發哀。

translations.literal: Among common folk in the lanes, whenever there is a heavy mourning they do not immediately raise the inquiry; first they visit the village altar, wait until all arrangements are ready, and only then begin wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Among common folk in the lanes, whenever there is a heavy mourning they do not immediately raise the inquiry; first they visit the village altar, wait until all arrangements are ready, and only then begin wailing.

sentences.zh: 至假車乘，雇棺槨，以榮送葬。

translations.literal: They even hire carriages and coffins to make the funeral procession glorious.
translations.idiomatic: They even hire carriages and coffins to make the funeral procession glorious.

sentences.zh: 既葬，鄰伍會集，相與酣醉，名曰出孝。

translations.literal: After burial the neighbors gather and drink together until drunk—calling it "bringing out mourning."
translations.idiomatic: After burial the neighbors gather and drink together until drunk—calling it "bringing out mourning."

sentences.zh: 夫婦之道，王化所基，故有三日不息燭、不舉樂之感。

translations.literal: The way of husband and wife is the foundation of royal transformation; hence the feeling of three days without extinguishing candles or raising music.
translations.idiomatic: The way of husband and wife is the foundation of royal transformation; hence the feeling of three days without extinguishing candles or raising music.

sentences.zh: 今昏嫁之初，雜奏絲竹，以窮宴歡。

translations.literal: Today at the start of marriage, string and bamboo are mixed in performance to exhaust all revelry.
translations.idiomatic: Today at the start of marriage, string and bamboo are mixed in performance to exhaust all revelry.

sentences.zh: 官司習俗，弗爲條禁。

translations.literal: Officialdom follows custom and makes no prohibitory statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Officialdom follows custom and makes no prohibitory statutes.

sentences.zh: 望一切懲革，申明禮憲。」

translations.literal: I hope all these may be punished and reformed, and the ritual code clearly declared.
translations.idiomatic: I hope all these may be punished and reformed, and the ritual code clearly declared.

sentences.zh: 俄復爲黃門侍郎，兼魏王泰府事。

translations.literal: Not long after he was again made Vice Director of the Department of the Imperial Household, concurrently administering the household of Prince Tai of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was again made Vice Director of the Department of the Imperial Household, concurrently administering the household of Prince Tai of Wei.

sentences.zh: 時泰有寵，太子多過失，帝密欲廢立，語杜正倫，正倫以漏言貶。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Tai was favored, the crown prince had many faults, and the emperor secretly wished to depose and install anew; he spoke to Du Zhenglun, and Du Zhenglun was demoted for leaking the words.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Tai was favored, the crown prince had many faults, and the emperor secretly wished to depose and install anew; he spoke to Du Zhenglun, and Du Zhenglun was demoted for leaking the words.

sentences.zh: 帝謂挺曰：「不忍復置卿於法。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wei Ting, "I cannot bear to place you under the law again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Wei Ting, "I cannot bear to place you under the law again.

sentences.zh: 改太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 初，挺爲大夫時，馬周爲監察御史，挺不甚禮。

translations.literal: At first, when Wei Ting was Censor-in-Chief, Ma Zhou was investigating censor, and Wei Ting did not show him much courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Wei Ting was Censor-in-Chief, Ma Zhou was investigating censor, and Wei Ting did not show him much courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及周爲中書令，帝欲湔拭用之，周言挺佷於自用，非宰相器，遂止。

translations.literal: When Ma Zhou became Director of the Secretariat, the emperor wished to cleanse and employ Wei Ting; Ma Zhou said Wei Ting was obstinate in self-will and not material for chancellor—the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Zhou became Director of the Secretariat, the emperor wished to cleanse and employ Wei Ting; Ma Zhou said Wei Ting was obstinate in self-will and not material for chancellor—the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 帝將討遼東，擇主餉運者。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to campaign against Liaodong and was choosing one to oversee provisions and transport.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to campaign against Liaodong and was choosing one to oversee provisions and transport.

sentences.zh: 周言挺才任粗使，帝謂然。

translations.literal: Zhou said Ting's talent was fit for rough service; the emperor said it was so.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou said that Ting's talents were fit only for coarse assignments, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 挺父故爲營州總管，嘗經略高麗，故劄藏家，挺上之。

translations.literal: Ting's late father had been governor-general of Yingzhou and had once conducted operations against Goguryeo; old maps were kept at home, and Ting presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's late father had served as governor-general of Yingzhou and had once campaigned against Goguryeo; old maps were kept in the family, and Ting presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝悅曰：「自幽距遼二千里無州縣，吾軍靡所仰食，卿爲朕圖之。

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "From Youzhou to Liaodong is two thousand li without prefectures or counties; our army has nowhere to rely for food—you must plan this for Us.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "From Youzhou to Liaodong stretches two thousand li without a single prefecture or county; our army has nowhere to draw its provisions—you must devise a plan for Us.

sentences.zh: 苟吾軍用不乏，是公之功。

translations.literal: If Our army's supplies are not lacking, that is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: If Our army's supplies never run short, that will be your achievement.

sentences.zh: 其自擇文武官四品十人爲子使，取幽、易、平三州銳士若馬各三百以從。」

translations.literal: Choose for yourself ten civil and military officials of the fourth rank as subordinate envoys, and take three hundred sharp soldiers and as many horses from each of the three prefectures of You, Yi, and Ping to follow you.
translations.idiomatic: Choose for yourself ten civil and military officials of the fourth rank to serve as your lieutenants, and take three hundred picked soldiers and as many horses from each of the three prefectures of You, Yi, and Ping.

sentences.zh: 即詔河北列州皆取挺節度，許以便宜。

translations.literal: An edict was immediately issued that all prefectures of Hebei should take orders from Ting, with discretionary authority granted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was immediately issued that all prefectures of Hebei should obey Ting's command, with discretionary powers granted.

sentences.zh: 帝親解貂裘及中廄馬賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally removed his sable fur coat and a horse from the central stables and bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally removed his sable fur coat and bestowed it on him, along with a horse from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 挺遣燕州司馬王安德行渠，作漕艫轉糧，自桑乾水抵盧思臺，行八百里，渠塞不可通。

translations.literal: Ting dispatched Wang An, assistant administrator of Yanzhou, to open a canal and build transport barges to move grain from the Sanggan River to Lusi Terrace, a distance of eight hundred li; the canal was blocked and could not be opened.
translations.idiomatic: Ting dispatched Wang An, assistant administrator of Yanzhou, to open a canal and build transport barges to move grain from the Sanggan River to Lusi Terrace—a distance of eight hundred li—but the canal was blocked and could not be opened.

sentences.zh: 挺以方苦寒，未可進，遂下米臺側，廥之，待凍泮乃運以爲解。

translations.literal: Ting judged that the cold was severe and advance was not yet possible, so he unloaded the grain beside the terrace, stored it in granaries, and planned to transport it once the ice thawed as a solution.
translations.idiomatic: Ting judged that the bitter cold made advance impossible, so he unloaded the grain beside the terrace, stored it in granaries, and planned to transport it once the ice thawed.

sentences.zh: 即上言：「度王師至，食且足。」

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized: "I estimate that when the imperial army arrives, provisions will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately memorialized, "I estimate that when the imperial army arrives, provisions will suffice.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅曰：「兵寧拙速，無工遲。

translations.literal: The emperor said displeased: "In war, better clumsy speed than skillful delay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said displeased, "In war, better clumsy speed than skillful delay.

sentences.zh: 我明年師出，挺乃度它歲運，何哉？」

translations.literal: Our army marches next year, yet Ting plans transport for another year—what is this?
translations.idiomatic: Our army marches next year—yet Ting plans transport for some other year. What is the meaning of this?

sentences.zh: 即詔繁畤令韋懷質馳按。

translations.literal: An edict was issued ordering Fanzhi magistrate Wei Huizhi to ride posthaste and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued ordering Fanzhi magistrate Wei Huizhi to ride posthaste and investigate.

sentences.zh: 懷質還劾：「挺在幽州，日置酒，弗憂職，不前視渠長利，即造船行粟，綿八百里，乃悟非是，欲進則不得，還且水涸。

translations.literal: Huizhi returned with impeachment charges: "Ting in Youzhou spends his days feasting, does not worry over his duties, did not first inspect whether the canal's length would serve, but at once built ships to transport grain over eight hundred li; only then did he realize his error, yet could not advance, and on the return journey the water had dried up.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi returned with impeachment charges: "Ting in Youzhou spends his days feasting and neglects his duties. He did not first inspect whether the canal's length would serve, but at once built ships to transport grain over eight hundred li; only then did he realize his error, yet could not advance, and on the return journey the water had already dried up.

sentences.zh: 六師所須，恐不如陛下之素。」

translations.literal: What the six armies require will probably fall short of Your Majesty's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: The requirements of the six armies will probably fall short of Your Majesty's expectations.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遣將少監李道裕代之。

translations.literal: The emperor in anger dispatched Vice Director of Palace Receptions Li Daoyu to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in anger dispatched Vice Director of Palace Receptions Li Daoyu to replace him.

sentences.zh: 敕治書侍御史唐臨馳傳，械挺赴洛陽，廢爲民，使白衣從。

translations.literal: He ordered Investigating Censor Tang Lin to ride posthaste, put Ting in fetters and escort him to Luoyang, stripped him of rank and made him a commoner, yet allowed him to follow in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Investigating Censor Tang Lin to ride posthaste, put Ting in fetters and escort him to Luoyang, stripped him of rank and made him a commoner, yet allowed him to follow in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 帝破蓋牟城，詔挺將兵鎮守，示復用。

translations.literal: When the emperor captured Gaimou Fortress, he ordered Ting to lead troops to garrison it, showing that he would be employed again.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor captured Gaimou Fortress, he ordered Ting to lead troops to garrison it—a sign that he would be employed again.

sentences.zh: 城與賊新城接，日夜轉鬥無休時。

translations.literal: The fortress adjoined the enemy's Xincheng, and day and night the fighting raged without respite.
translations.idiomatic: The fortress adjoined the enemy's Xincheng, and day and night the fighting raged without respite.

sentences.zh: 挺以失職，內不平，作書謝所善公孫常。

translations.literal: Ting, having lost his office, felt inwardly aggrieved and wrote a letter to his friend Gongsun Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Ting, having lost his office, felt inwardly aggrieved and wrote a letter to his friend Gongsun Chang.

sentences.zh: 常，善數者也，以他事系，投繯死。

translations.literal: Chang, who was skilled in divination, had been detained on another matter and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, who was skilled in divination, had been detained on another matter and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 索橐中得挺書，言所屯危蹙，意怨望，貶象州刺史。

translations.literal: In searching his belongings they found Ting's letter, which spoke of his garrison's peril and distress and betrayed resentment; he was demoted to prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In searching his belongings they found Ting's letter, which spoke of his garrison's peril and distress and betrayed resentment; he was demoted to prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: More than a year later he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he died, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子待價、萬石。

translations.literal: His sons were Daijia and Wanshi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Daijia and Wanshi.

sentences.zh: 挺子 待價待價，初爲左千牛備身，永徽中，江夏王道宗得罪，待價以婿貶盧龍府果毅。

translations.literal: Ting's son Daijia—Daijia at first served as a Left Palace Guard attendant; in the Yonghui era, when the Prince of Jiangxia, Li Daozong, fell from favor, Daijia, as his son-in-law, was demoted to captain of Lulong District.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's son Daijia—Daijia at first served as a Left Palace Guard attendant; in the Yonghui era, when the Prince of Jiangxia, Li Daozong, fell from favor, Daijia, as his son-in-law, was demoted to captain of Lulong District.

sentences.zh: 時將軍辛文陵招慰高麗，次吐護真水，爲虜所襲，待價與中郎將薛仁貴率所部兵殺之，文陵亦苦戰，遂免。

translations.literal: At that time General Xin Wenling was pacifying Goguryeo and encamped at the Tuhuzhen River, where he was attacked by the enemy; Daijia with General of the Palace Guard Xue Rengui led their troops and killed them, Wenling also fought bitterly, and they escaped danger.
translations.idiomatic: At that time General Xin Wenling was pacifying Goguryeo and encamped at the Tuhuzhen River, where he was attacked by the enemy; Daijia with General of the Palace Guard Xue Rengui led their troops and killed them, Wenling also fought bitterly, and they escaped danger.

sentences.zh: 待價重創，矢著左足，隱不言，卒以疾免。

translations.literal: Daijia was severely wounded, an arrow lodged in his left foot, which he concealed and did not report; he was eventually dismissed on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Daijia was severely wounded, an arrow lodged in his left foot, which he concealed and did not report; he was eventually dismissed on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 起爲蘭州刺史。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃盜邊，高宗以沛王賢爲涼州大都督，而待價爲司馬。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans raided the frontier, Emperor Gaozong made Prince Pei Xian governor-general of Liangzhou, with Daijia as his vice administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans raided the frontier, Emperor Gaozong made Prince Pei Xian governor-general of Liangzhou, with Daijia as his vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 俄遷肅州刺史，以功召拜右武衞將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be prefect of Suzhou; for his achievements he was summoned and appointed General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to be prefect of Suzhou; for his achievements he was summoned and appointed General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年，吐蕃復入寇，以待價檢校涼州都督，兼知鎮守兵馬事。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Yifeng era, when the Tibetans again invaded, Daijia was made acting governor of Liangzhou and concurrently charged with garrison troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yifeng era, when the Tibetans again invaded, Daijia was made acting governor of Liangzhou and concurrently charged with garrison troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 召還，封扶陽侯。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 武后臨朝，攝司空，護營乾陵，改天官尚書、同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, he served as acting Minister of Works, supervised construction of the Qianling tomb, and was made Minister of the Heavenly Office and Third Rank of the Phoenix Gate and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, he served as acting Minister of Works, supervised construction of the Qianling tomb, and was made Minister of the Heavenly Office and Third Rank of the Phoenix Gate and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 待價起武力，典選無銓總才，故朝野共蚩薄之。

translations.literal: Daijia had risen through military prowess and had no talent for overall management of appointments, so court and country alike looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Daijia had risen through military prowess and had no talent for overall management of appointments, so court and country alike looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 俄爲燕然道行軍大總管，禦突厥。

translations.literal: Soon he was made commander-in-chief of the campaign route to Mount Yanran to repel the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commander-in-chief of the campaign route to Mount Yanran to repel the Turks.

sentences.zh: 逾年還，拜文昌右相、同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned and was appointed Right Chancellor of the Directorate of Literature and Third Rank of the Phoenix Gate and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he returned and was appointed Right Chancellor of the Directorate of Literature and Third Rank of the Phoenix Gate and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 不自安，累表辭職，不聽。

translations.literal: Ill at ease, he repeatedly submitted memorials resigning; his requests were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Ill at ease, he repeatedly submitted memorials resigning; his requests were not granted.

sentences.zh: 且請盡力行陣，許之，於是拜安息道行軍大總管，督三十六總管以討吐蕃，進爵公。

translations.literal: He also petitioned to serve fully in the field; this was granted, and he was then appointed commander-in-chief of the Anxi campaign route, directing thirty-six commanders against the Tibetans, and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to serve fully in the field; this was granted, and he was then appointed commander-in-chief of the Anxi campaign route, directing thirty-six commanders against the Tibetans, and advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 軍至寅識迦河，與吐蕃合戰，勝負略相當。

translations.literal: The army reached the Yinshijia River and joined battle with the Tibetans; victory and defeat were roughly even.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached the Yinshijia River and joined battle with the Tibetans; victory and defeat were roughly even.

sentences.zh: 會其副閻溫古逗留，又天大寒，待價不善撫御，師人多死，餉道乏，乃旋師頓高昌。

translations.literal: But his deputy Yan Wengu dallied, and the weather turned bitterly cold; Daijia was poor at keeping his troops in hand, many soldiers died, supplies ran out, and he withdrew to encamp at Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: But his deputy Yan Wengu dallied, and the weather turned bitterly cold; Daijia was poor at keeping his troops in hand, many soldiers died, supplies ran out, and he withdrew to encamp at Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 後大怒，斬溫古，流待價繡州，卒。

translations.literal: Later the empress was greatly angered, executed Wengu, and banished Daijia to Xiuzhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later the empress was greatly angered, executed Wengu, and banished Daijia to Xiuzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 挺玄孫 武曾孫武。

translations.literal: Ting's great-great-grandson Wu—Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's great-great-grandson was Wu.

sentences.zh: 武少孤。

translations.literal: Wu lost his father while young.
translations.idiomatic: Wu lost his father while young.

sentences.zh: 年十一，廕補右千牛，累遷長安丞。

translations.literal: At eleven he inherited appointment as a Right Palace Guard and rose through successive posts to aide of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he inherited appointment as a Right Palace Guard and rose through successive posts to aide of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸梁州，委妻子奔行在，除殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong went to Liangzhou, Wu left wife and children and rushed to the imperial encampment, and was appointed Palace Assistant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong went to Liangzhou, Wu left wife and children and rushed to the imperial encampment, and was appointed Palace Assistant Censor.

sentences.zh: 戸部侍郎元琇爲水陸轉運使，表武以倉部員外郎充判官。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister of Revenue Yuan Xiu served as commissioner for land and water transport, he recommended Wu as his aide in the capacity of Vice Director of the Granary Department.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister of Revenue Yuan Xiu served as commissioner for land and water transport, he recommended Wu as his aide in the capacity of Vice Director of the Granary Department.

sentences.zh: 謀不用，杜門數月而琇敗。

translations.literal: His plans were not adopted; he shut his doors for several months, and then Xiu fell from power.
translations.idiomatic: His plans were not adopted; he shut his doors for several months, and then Xiu fell from power.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝以反正告郊廟，大兵後，典章苟完，執事者時時咨武。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had announced the restoration at the suburban altars; after the great wars, though the rites and regulations were barely intact, those in charge frequently consulted Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had announced the restoration at the suburban altars; after the great wars, though the rites and regulations were barely intact, those in charge frequently consulted Wu.

sentences.zh: 武酌宜約用，得禮之衷，群司奉焉。

translations.literal: Wu weighed what was suitable and applied it with restraint, obtaining the core of ritual, and the various offices followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu weighed what was suitable and applied it with restraint, hitting the heart of ritual propriety, and the various offices followed his lead.

sentences.zh: 後爲絳州刺史，鑿汾水灌田萬三千餘頃，璽書勞勉。

translations.literal: Later as prefect of Jiangzhou he cut channels from the Fen River to irrigate more than thirteen thousand qing of fields, and received an imperial letter of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Later as prefect of Jiangzhou he cut channels from the Fen River to irrigate more than thirteen thousand qing of fields, and received an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，入爲京兆尹，護治豐陵，未成，卒，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xianzong he entered court as chief administrator of the capital region, supervised construction of Fengling tomb, died before it was finished, and was posthumously made Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong he entered court as chief administrator of the capital region, supervised construction of Fengling tomb, died before it was finished, and was posthumously made Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 挺子 萬石萬石，頗涉學，善音律。

translations.literal: Ting's son Wanshi—Wanshi was broadly learned and skilled in music.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's son Wanshi—Wanshi was broadly learned and skilled in music.

sentences.zh: 上元中，遷累太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he rose through successive posts to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era he rose through successive posts to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 當時郊廟燕會樂曲，皆萬石與太史令姚元辯增損之，號任職。

translations.literal: At that time the music for suburban sacrifices, temple rites, and banquet gatherings was all augmented and reduced by Wanshi together with Court Astronomer Yao Yuanbian, and he was called diligent in office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the music for suburban sacrifices, temple rites, and banquet gatherings was all revised by Wanshi together with Court Astronomer Yao Yuanbian, and he was praised as diligent in office.

sentences.zh: 始，萬石奏「太樂博士弟子遭喪者，先無它業，請以卒哭追集」。

translations.literal: At first Wanshi memorialized: "Students of the Grand Music Master who suffer bereavement, having no other occupation, should be recalled after the end of mourning."
translations.idiomatic: At first Wanshi memorialized: "Students of the Grand Music Master who suffer bereavement, having no other occupation, should be recalled after the end of mourning."

sentences.zh: 侍御史劉思立劾奏萬石曰：「移風易俗，莫善於樂；

translations.literal: Censor Liu Sili impeached Wanshi, saying: "Of all means to transform custom and reform manners, none surpasses music;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Sili impeached Wanshi, saying, "Of all means to transform custom and reform manners, none surpasses music;

sentences.zh: 睦親化人，莫善於孝。

translations.literal: To harmonize kin and transform the people, none surpasses filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: to harmonize kin and transform the people, none surpasses filial piety.

sentences.zh: 所以三年之禮，天下通喪。

translations.literal: Hence the rites of three years' mourning are universal throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the rites of three years' mourning are universal throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 今遣音聲人釋服爲樂，帶絰治音，豈以小人不能執禮，遂欲約爲非法？

translations.literal: Now you send musicians to lay aside mourning garb and perform music, wearing hemp bands while regulating musical affairs—is it because common men cannot observe ritual that you wish to reduce it to something unlawful?
translations.idiomatic: Now you send musicians to lay aside mourning garb and perform music, wearing hemp bands while regulating musical affairs—is it because common men cannot observe ritual that you wish to reduce it to something unlawful?

sentences.zh: 萬石官太常，首紊風化，請付吏論罪。」

translations.literal: Wanshi holds office as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices yet leads in corrupting custom and teaching; I ask that he be handed over to the officials for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Wanshi holds office as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices yet leads in corrupting custom and teaching; I ask that he be handed over to the officials for judgment.

sentences.zh: 高宗方委任萬石，罷其奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong was then placing trust in Wanshi and dismissed the impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong was then placing trust in Wanshi and dismissed the impeachment.

sentences.zh: 後知吏部選事，卒於官。

translations.literal: Later he oversaw appointments in the Ministry of Personnel and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he oversaw appointments in the Ministry of Personnel and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：王者用人非難，盡其才之爲難。

translations.literal: The encomium says: For a king to employ men is not difficult; exhausting their talents is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: For a sovereign to employ men is not difficult; to exhaust their talents is difficult.

sentences.zh: 觀太宗之責任也，謀斯從，言斯聽，才斯奮，洞然不疑，故人臣未始遺力，天子高拱操成功，致太平矣。

translations.literal: Observing how Emperor Taizong charged responsibility: when he plotted, it was followed; when he spoke, it was heard; talents were roused; he was clear and without doubt—hence ministers never left strength unused, the Son of Heaven sat elevated with folded hands yet achieved success, and great peace was attained.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how Emperor Taizong charged his men: counsel he followed, words he heeded, talents he unleashed, with clear vision and no doubt—hence ministers never held back their strength, the Son of Heaven sat elevated with folded hands yet achieved success, and great peace was attained.

sentences.zh: 始皆奮亡命布衣，嬪然列置上袞。

translations.literal: At first they were all men who had striven as outlaws in plain cloth, yet were arrayed in succession among the highest robes.
translations.idiomatic: At first they were all daring men who had risked their lives, commoners in plain cloth—yet they were arranged in succession among the highest rank.

sentences.zh: 薛收雖早夭，帝本以中書令待之。

translations.literal: Though Xue Shou died young, the emperor had originally intended to treat him as Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xue Shou died young, the emperor had intended to treat him as Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 御臣之方，顧不善哉！

translations.literal: His way of governing ministers—was it not excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Was his way of governing ministers not admirable!

sentences.zh: 挺晩節流落，蓋有致而然。

translations.literal: That Ting in his later years fell to ruin—surely there were causes for it.
translations.idiomatic: That Ting in his later years fell to ruin was surely something he brought upon himself.
